title: Purpose of enterprises
context: Assess the following statements on the purpose of enterprises:
statements: Enterprises are regarded as economically independent organisational units that produce goods and services not only for themselves but for others.
The purpose of an enterprise includes recognising or stimulating the needs of private households, other enterprises or the state and providing suitable offers.
A technically flawless offer is generally purchased even when customers see no value or benefit of their own in it.
Enterprises typically address their offer only to end consumers; supplier relationships and public contracting authorities fall outside the circle of addressees.
Without recognisable value and benefit for customers, purchase interest generally fails to arise; that is precisely why creating this benefit is important for enterprises.
tactical_explanations:
Independent and for third parties: that is what distinguishes enterprises from pure production for own use. The organisational unit produces goods or services for others — households, businesses or the state. Anyone who manufactures only for their own consumption does not fulfil this role.

The statement is true.

The purpose is needs orientation, not producing for the sake of producing. Private households, other enterprises and the state stand side by side as possible demanders. Dropping one group narrows the mandate impermissibly.

The statement is true.

Technical quality alone is not enough. Purchase interest arises when customers recognise value and benefit in the offer. Without that impression, even a fault-free product often remains unsaleable.

The statement is false.

End consumers are only one group of addressees. Suppliers sell to enterprises, and public bodies are demanders as well. Restricting the circle to households alone contradicts the wider set of addressees.

The statement is false.

Value and benefit are the bridge to purchase. Because interest and the buying decision hang on them, it is central for enterprises to create exactly this customer benefit — not an arbitrary offer with no link to buyers.

The statement is true.

title: Input factors of performance creation
context: Assess the following statements on what enterprises deploy for performance creation:
statements: The inputs of performance creation include means of production such as machinery and business equipment.
Materials — for example raw materials — are among the means that enterprises deploy for performance creation.
In this context, labour means only physical assembly-line work; planning know-how and information do not count as inputs.
When enterprises employ staff, they thereby create jobs.
When businesses compete and develop their offer further, innovations can arise from that.
tactical_explanations:
Means of production are not extras: machinery and business equipment flow directly into performance creation — alongside materials, staff, and know-how and information.

The statement is true.

Raw materials are a typical example of materials. Without material inputs, production often could not take place; materials therefore stand on equal footing with means of production and staff.

The statement is true.

Labour means the work performance of staff as a whole. Know-how and information are separate inputs alongside it. Narrowing this to assembly-line work would leave out service providers and knowledge work.

The statement is false.

Employment has an immediate labour-market effect: when employees are hired, jobs are created. That follows from the staff-input side of performance creation.

The statement is true.

Competition and ongoing further development go together. Innovations arise here above all when businesses continually adapt their offer and develop something new — not through standstill.

The statement is true.

title: Statutory definition in the UGB
context: Assess the following statements on the statutory definition of enterprises in the Unternehmensgesetzbuch:
statements: Under § 1(1) UGB, an entrepreneur is anyone who operates an enterprise.
§ 1(2) UGB describes an enterprise as a permanently organised set-up for independent economic activity — even if it is not directed at profit.
A single sale without a permanently organised set-up is already enough for the statutory definition of an enterprise.
The UGB definition requires that every enterprise be oriented toward making a profit.
Independent economic activity includes producing goods and/or services for third parties at one's own risk.
tactical_explanations:
Paragraph 1 links entrepreneur status to operating an enterprise. Without an enterprise being operated, that legal status is missing — regardless of turnover or headcount.

The statement is true.

Paragraph 2 fills out the concept of an enterprise: permanence, independent economic activity, and the explicit openness even without a profit orientation. Non-profit structures can fall under it if the other features fit.

The statement is true.

"Permanently organised" rules out purely one-off action. A flea-market sale on one afternoon without a lasting organisation does not meet the definition.

The statement is false.

Profit intent is allowed but not required. The definition admits activities that need not be directed at profit. A duty of profit orientation would exclude non-profit organisations unnecessarily.

The statement is false.

Independent, for third parties and at one's own risk: that is the core of economic activity. Pure own consumption or dependent performance in someone else's name is not enough.

The statement is true.

title: woom, Manner and the three features
context: woom GmbH manufactures bicycles; Josef Manner & Comp. AG manufactures wafers and other confectionery. Assess the following statements:
statements: woom and Manner are permanently organised because bicycles and wafers are not produced only temporarily for a few days.
Both businesses bear entrepreneurial risk and produce for third parties.
Without an express profit intent, woom and Manner could not legally count as enterprises.
From a business-economics perspective, an enterprise is economically active when it provides services for third parties.
If an enterprise can permanently neither cover its costs nor remain solvent, it loses its basis for existence from a business-economics perspective.
tactical_explanations:
Permanence shows in ongoing production, not in a flea market's day-to-day business. Bicycle and wafer production are set up for continuity.

The statement is true.

Both features apply: entrepreneurial risk and performance creation for third parties. Alongside permanence, they thus also meet the further enterprise features.

The statement is true.

Profit intent is not a legal prerequisite. Both businesses are in fact run with profit intent, but they would not need to be in order to count as enterprises.

The statement is false.

The business-economics reading emphasises performance for third parties. Own needs alone do not yet establish an enterprise in this sense.

The statement is true.

Cost coverage and solvency secure continuity. If both are permanently missing, the business-economics basis for existence falls away — regardless of whether a legal organisation still exists.

The statement is true.

title: Profits and continuity
context: Assess the following statements on profits in enterprises:
statements: Simplified, profits mean more receipts than expenditures, or in accounting terms more revenues than expenses.
For continuity, profits are generally essential because they can be reinvested.
Reinvested profits support performance and competitiveness and reduce the risk of over-indebtedness in loss phases.
A profit once achieved practically rules out later loss phases.
Profits must be fully distributed and may not remain in the enterprise.
tactical_explanations:
The simplified and the accounting views mean the same core: a surplus of revenues over expenses. That is profit — not mere turnover level.

The statement is true.

Reinvestment keeps businesses capable of performing. Without a return flow into the enterprise, the capacity for renewal and a crisis buffer is often missing.

The statement is true.

When profits remain in the enterprise, they strengthen equity and resilience. In loss years that cushion works against over-indebtedness.

The statement is true.

A profit year does not end entrepreneurial risk. Later losses remain possible; profit is not a permanent state.

The statement is false.

Distribution is an option, not a duty. Profits can — and often should — remain in the enterprise and be reinvested.

The statement is false.

title: Non-profit organisations
context: Assess the following statements on non-profit organisations:
statements: A non-profit organisation is primarily oriented toward cost coverage, not profit maximisation.
Adequate receipts — for example donations — help an NPO pursue its goals better and communicate its offer more clearly to the target group.
NPOs may generate no receipts at all, because any receipt would automatically turn them into profit-oriented enterprises.
NPOs too can benefit from reinvested surpluses by improving and expanding their offer.
Because an NPO works primarily on a cost-covering basis, it cannot legally be an enterprise.
tactical_explanations:
Non-profit does not mean "without economic activity", but primarily cost coverage rather than profit maximisation. That remains the orientation point.

The statement is true.

Without adequate means, fulfilment of the task stalls. Donations and similar receipts strengthen reach and communication — even without a profit purpose.

The statement is true.

Receipts are usual and necessary for NPOs. They do not automatically make the organisation profit-oriented; what matters remains the purpose orientation.

The statement is false.

Surpluses can flow back into the offer. Reinvestment improves services without profit maximisation having to follow as the purpose.

The statement is true.

Legally, organisations not directed at profit can also be enterprises if permanence and independent economic activity are present. Cost coverage does not exclude the concept of an enterprise.

The statement is false.

title: Value added in the production process
context: Assess the following statements on the value added of enterprises:
statements: In the production or service process, goods arise with a higher value than the intermediate inputs originally deployed.
From a business-economics perspective, this value difference is the enterprise's value added.
Value added and profit are the same thing, because both denote the difference between turnover and all costs.
Value added results as the difference between the value of the end product and the value of the intermediate inputs deployed.
Intermediate inputs are purchased components and materials that the enterprise does not manufacture itself.
tactical_explanations:
Value added arises in the process: the result is worth more than the inputs. That applies equally to products and services.

The statement is true.

The business-economics reading equates value added with this value difference — not with accounting profit.

The statement is true.

Profit deducts all costs; value added deducts only intermediate inputs from the end value. Staff, depreciation and other costs still lie in between.

The statement is false.

End value minus intermediate inputs: that is the calculation formula for value added. Supplier values stay outside.

The statement is true.

What is purchased and not produced in-house counts as an intermediate input. Own manufacture of the same parts would not be an intermediate input in this sense.

The statement is true.

title: Children's bicycle and 400 euros of value added
context: An enterprise manufactures a children's bicycle worth 500 euros. The purchased intermediate inputs amount to around 100 euros. Assess the following statements:
statements: With an end value of 500 euros and intermediate inputs of 100 euros, value added amounts to 400 euros.
The 400 euros of value added are at the same time the profit per bicycle.
Value added = 500 euros end value minus 100 euros intermediate inputs.
Beyond the intermediate inputs, further costs arise before one can speak of profit.
Because the finished bike is worth 500 euros, value added amounts to 500 euros; purchased parts remain disregarded.
tactical_explanations:
500 minus 100 equals 400. Exactly this difference is the value added in the example.

The statement is true.

Value added is not profit. Wages, depreciation and further costs still have to be covered before a surplus remains.

The statement is false.

The calculation follows the definition: end value minus intermediate inputs. Here clearly 500 − 100.

The statement is true.

Intermediate inputs are only one cost block. Without covering the remaining costs there is no profit — even with positive value added.

The statement is true.

Taking the end value alone as value added would forget the intermediate inputs. Without deducting the 100 euros, the figure would be wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Value added and gross domestic product
context: Assess the following statements on the link between value added and GDP:
statements: Value added is relevant for calculating GDP because it represents the generation of GDP.
The basis of GDP calculation is the total value of goods produced domestically minus intermediate inputs.
In this logic, GDP corresponds to enterprises' turnover without deducting intermediate inputs.
Without deducting intermediate inputs, supplier values would enter the macroeconomic aggregate multiple times.
As generation of GDP, only enterprise profit counts, not value added.
tactical_explanations:
GDP arises from value added. The macroeconomic aggregate builds on this difference, not on raw turnovers.

The statement is true.

Domestic production minus intermediate inputs: that is how double counting is avoided and the generation of GDP is depicted.

The statement is true.

Turnover without deducting intermediate inputs would count supplies multiple times. GDP works with value added, not with gross turnover.

The statement is false.

Supplier values would otherwise reappear at every stage. Deducting intermediate inputs prevents exactly this multiple counting.

The statement is true.

Profit is narrower than value added. For GDP generation, value added counts, not profit alone.

The statement is false.

title: Primary economic sector
context: Assess the following statements on the primary sector:
statements: The primary sector includes the extraction of raw materials, in particular agriculture and forestry, fisheries and mining.
The extraction of ores from which metals later arise counts toward the primary sector.
Cultivation as well as harvesting of fruit belong to the primary sector.
Agricultural businesses that supply nuts to Manner operate in the primary sector.
A tax adviser who prepares balance sheets counts toward the primary sector because data are the "raw materials" of advice.
tactical_explanations:
Primary means raw-material extraction and primary production — not processing and not services.

The statement is true.

Ore mining is extraction; metal production is only processing. The extraction itself remains primary.

The statement is true.

Agricultural production of fruit is classic primary production and therefore primary.

The statement is true.

Nut suppliers engage in agriculture or raw-material provision — primary sector, even if the buyer processes industrially.

The statement is true.

Tax advice is a service and belongs to the tertiary sector. The metaphor "figures as raw materials" does not change the sector logic.

The statement is false.

title: Secondary sector and processing
context: Assess the following statements on the secondary economic sector:
statements: The secondary sector processes raw materials into products and comprises industry, crafts and the energy industry.
Extracting metal from ores or producing a wafer filling from cocoa and hazelnuts counts toward the secondary sector.
Mechanical engineering, electronics and chemical products belong to the secondary sector.
woom and Manner are secondarily active because they produce products from raw materials and components.
A bicycle retailer with woom bikes in its range counts toward the secondary sector because the bikes traded are industrial products.
tactical_explanations:
Processing and manufacture characterise the secondary sector — including crafts and energy, not only large-scale industry.

The statement is true.

From raw material to product: that is exactly secondary activity, whether metal or confectionery filling.

The statement is true.

These industries produce physical goods from intermediate inputs and raw materials and thus clearly lie in the secondary sector.

The statement is true.

Both produce end products from inputs — classic secondary performance, not pure trading or advisory performance.

The statement is true.

Trade is a service and therefore tertiary. That the goods were manufactured industrially does not make the retailer a producer.

The statement is false.

title: Tertiary sector and services
context: Assess the following statements on the tertiary sector:
statements: The tertiary sector comprises services such as trade, tourism, legal and tax advice, banks and insurance.
Care, education as well as coaching and training count among tertiary services.
A tax adviser who prepares enterprise balance sheets operates in the tertiary sector.
Tourism counts toward the primary sector because landscapes are natural resources.
As a country's economic development rises, the tertiary sector's share of economic output generally rises.
tactical_explanations:
Services of all kinds — from trade to financial services — form the tertiary sector.

The statement is true.

Person-related and education-related services are likewise services and therefore tertiary.

The statement is true.

Balance-sheet advice is neither raw-material extraction nor industrial manufacture, but a service.

The statement is true.

Tourism uses nature but does not produce it. The performance remains a service and therefore tertiary.

The statement is false.

Higher development typically goes with more demand for services; the tertiary share grows.

The statement is true.

title: Sector shares in Austria
context: Assess the following statements on the shares of the economic sectors in Austria:
statements: In Austria the tertiary sector contributes around 70 percent of economic output.
The primary sector contributes a little over 1 percent of economic output in Austria.
Because the primary share of economic output is small, it barely matters for food supply and care of nature.
woom and Manner are to be assigned to the tertiary sector because services make up around 70 percent in Austria.
The object of the enterprise determines in which sector or sectors a business operates.
tactical_explanations:
The order of magnitude of around 70 percent for the tertiary share of Austrian economic output is the relevant reference figure.

The statement is true.

A little over 1 percent: the primary share of economic output is small, despite its importance for supply.

The statement is true.

Share of economic output and societal importance diverge. Supply and care of nature remain central even with a small GDP share.

The statement is false.

Sector assignment follows the object of the enterprise, not the macroeconomic sector share. Producers remain secondary.

The statement is false.

What the business does determines the sector — not the legal form and not the national average of sector shares.

The statement is true.

title: Industries and branches of the economy
context: Assess the following statements on the industry affiliation of enterprises:
statements: The field of activity determines which industry or industries an enterprise is assigned to.
Within an industry, enterprises manufacture very similar products or create very similar services.
Construction, crafts, trade, pharma and health, telecommunications, tourism, hospitality, transport and logistics as well as media are typical industry examples.
Every enterprise can be assigned to only exactly one industry; multiple affiliation is ruled out.
Interest representations often follow industry logic because businesses in one industry share similar challenges and interests.
tactical_explanations:
Industry follows what the business does — the field of activity — not the legal form alone.

The statement is true.

Similar services and products characterise the same branch of the economy. That is exactly why challenges cluster.

The statement is true.

The list shows typical industries; it is illustrative, not exhaustive.

The statement is true.

Enterprises can belong to several industries if the field of activity supports that. There is no forced single assignment.

The statement is false.

Shared interests explain why associations are organised by industry.

The statement is true.

title: SMEs and size classes
context: Assess the following statements on classifying enterprises by size:
statements: Size classes matter because tax rules, accounting duties and subsidies can be tied to enterprise size.
SME stands for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (Engl. SME/MSME) and is defined in an EU recommendation.
Micro-enterprises have up to 9 employees and turnover or balance-sheet total of up to 2 million euros.
A business with 250 employees still counts among medium-sized enterprises under the EU recommendation.
Medium-sized enterprises reach up to 249 employees, up to 50 million euros turnover or up to 43 million euros balance-sheet total; large ones begin from 250 employees.
tactical_explanations:
Size steers duties and opportunities: taxes, accounting and subsidies often attach to class boundaries.

The statement is true.

SME is the collective term below large enterprises and is defined by EU recommendation.

The statement is true.

The micro thresholds are tight: at most 9 persons and at most 2 million euros for turnover or balance-sheet total.

The statement is true.

From 250 employees the class of large enterprises begins — regardless of whether turnover still looks "medium".

The statement is false.

249 remains medium, 250 is large. The turnover and balance-sheet total limits of the medium class lie at 50 and 43 million euros respectively.

The statement is true.

title: SMEs in Austria
context: Assess the following statements on the importance of SMEs in Austria:
statements: In Austria SMEs make up around 99 percent of the number of enterprises.
Micro-enterprises with fewer than ten employees make up around 90 percent of the number of enterprises.
Around two thirds of employed persons work in SMEs; these generate just under two thirds of the turnover of the commercial economy.
A little more than one third of turnover falls to around 1,900 large enterprises.
Because SMEs make up around 99 percent of the number of enterprises, around 99 percent of turnover also falls to micro-enterprises with less than one million euros of turnover.
tactical_explanations:
Numerical dominance of SMEs: around 99 percent of businesses — as in the EU overall.

The statement is true.

Among SMEs, micro businesses predominate; around 90 percent of all enterprises have under ten employees.

The statement is true.

Employment and turnover share of SMEs each lie at about two thirds — important, but not identical with the 99 percent count.

The statement is true.

A few large enterprises account for over one third of turnover. Count and turnover share diverge.

The statement is true.

Dominance by count does not mean turnover dominance of micro businesses. Large enterprises and larger SMEs carry substantial turnover shares.

The statement is false.

title: Stakeholder groups and interaction
context: Assess the following statements on enterprises' stakeholder groups:
statements: Enterprises influence several groups of people and their environment — and are themselves influenced by these.
Stakeholder groups (stakeholders) have expectations of the enterprise.
In practice, stakeholder groups primarily include the owners; employees, suppliers and customers do not count among them.
The enterprise itself also has expectations of its stakeholder groups.
Influence runs only from the business outward; there are no feedback effects of the groups on the enterprise.
tactical_explanations:
Stakeholder relationships are mutual: influence runs in both directions.

The statement is true.

The groups' expectations of the business are the core of the stakeholder concept.

The statement is true.

Owners are only one group. Staff, suppliers, customers, capital providers and the location also count.

The statement is false.

Reciprocity: the business expects e.g. performance, payment or cooperation from the groups.

The statement is true.

Feedback effects belong to it — for example via demand, financing or location policy. A one-way street would be wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Employees' expectations
context: Assess the following statements on the expectations of employees:
statements: Employees want a secure, interesting and well-paid job.
Employees are a stakeholder group because the enterprise influences them and depends on their work performance.
For staff, what mainly counts is the highest possible price of the end products, not their own position.
Job security stands alongside interest in the work as well as pay in the same set of expectations.
Once someone is employed, any interest in the further development of the job ceases.
tactical_explanations:
Secure, interesting, well paid: those are the typical staff expectations of the employer.

The statement is true.

Dependence and influence establish employees' stakeholder role.

The statement is true.

End-product prices are a customer topic. Staff mainly expect conditions of their own position.

The statement is false.

The three aspects stand side by side, not as substitutes for one another.

The statement is true.

Employment does not end interest in development, security and pay.

The statement is false.

title: Suppliers as a stakeholder group
context: Assess the following statements on the expectations of suppliers:
statements: Suppliers want a good business relationship.
They want punctual and complete payment for their deliveries.
Because suppliers receive a fee, they are not a stakeholder group.
Late as well as only partial payment fulfils the suppliers' stated wish.
The enterprise influences its suppliers and is itself influenced by the supply relationship.
tactical_explanations:
A good business relationship is a central supplier expectation alongside payment.

The statement is true.

Punctual and complete: that is the payment wish on the supply side.

The statement is true.

A fee changes nothing about the stakeholder role. Expectations remain.

The statement is false.

Late and incomplete contradicts exactly the wish for punctual full payment.

The statement is false.

Reciprocity also applies in the supply chain.

The statement is true.

title: Customer expectations of performance and price
context: Assess the following statements on the expectations of customers:
statements: Customers want good products and services at a favourable price.
Customers count among the stakeholder groups even if they hold no shares in the enterprise.
Customers mainly want expensive services of low quality, because only a high price signals value.
Good performance and a favourable price stand side by side in customer expectations.
Only the state as demander counts as customers; private households and other enterprises fall out of the buyer role.
tactical_explanations:
Quality and value for money at once: that is the typical customer expectation.

The statement is true.

Shareholder status is not a prerequisite for buyers' stakeholder role.

The statement is true.

Expensive and poor contradicts the stated expectation. Price can signal quality but does not replace it as a wish.

The statement is false.

Both are demanded — not as mutually exclusive opposites.

The statement is true.

Households, enterprises and the state can be buyers. Restricting this to the state is wrong.

The statement is false.

title: Owners, shareholders and financiers
context: Assess the following statements on owners, shareholders and financiers:
statements: Owners, shareholders as well as financiers hope for good development of the enterprise.
With the money invested they also pursue certain goals.
Once capital has been contributed, these groups no longer have any interest in the further course of the business.
Ownership, company shares and other financiers stand side by side as capital-provider roles.
Only employees deploy money and pursue goals with it; owners remain unmentioned.
tactical_explanations:
Capital providers hope for positive enterprise development — that connects the roles.

The statement is true.

Capital deployment is goal-directed: return, influence, security or similar.

The statement is true.

After the contribution, interest in the course remains; capital is not a one-off pay-off.

The statement is false.

The list covers ownership, shareholders and further financiers, not only one role.

The statement is true.

Employees mainly deploy work performance. Capital deployment characterises owners and financiers.

The statement is false.

title: Municipality, federal state and location
context: Assess the following statements on municipalities and the federal state as stakeholder groups:
statements: Municipality and federal state benefit from jobs and levies of the resident enterprise.
They expect the enterprise to meet its financial as well as other obligations.
The location does not count among the stakeholder groups because only market parties can be stakeholders.
Alongside the municipality, the federal state in which the business is based is also named.
Jobs and levies are of no great importance for the location.
tactical_explanations:
Location benefit: employment and levies. That is why municipality and federal state are stakeholder groups.

The statement is true.

Meeting obligations belongs to location expectations — financially and beyond.

The statement is true.

Stakeholders are not limited to market parties. The location belongs among them.

The statement is false.

Municipality and federal state stand in parallel as territorial authorities of residence.

The statement is true.

Exactly jobs and levies establish the location benefit — they are central, not secondary.

The statement is false.

title: Environment and social responsibility
context: Assess the following statements on environment and societal responsibility of enterprises:
statements: Municipality and federal state expect careful, responsible handling of the environment.
They also expect the enterprise to exercise social responsibility toward society.
Environmental conduct and social responsibility do not belong among location expectations.
Financial and other obligations stand in the same set of expectations as environment and society.
In practice, social responsibility is directed only at the shareholders, not at society as a whole.
tactical_explanations:
Environmental care is an explicit location expectation alongside levies and jobs.

The statement is true.

Social responsibility toward society belongs to it as well.

The statement is true.

Both topics are part of location expectations, not a side note.

The statement is false.

Obligations, environment and society stand in one set of expectations.

The statement is true.

The expectation is directed at the enterprise toward society — not only at internal shareholder interests.

The statement is false.

title: Mutual expectations
context: Assess the following statements on reciprocity between enterprises and stakeholder groups:
statements: Stakeholder groups have expectations of the enterprise, and the enterprise has expectations of the stakeholder groups.
Once a group counts as a stakeholder, the enterprise may no longer expect any counterpart performance at all.
The interaction covers staff, the supply chain, buyers, capital providers and the location at once.
The technical term stakeholder groups is equated with stakeholders.
Only large enterprises from 250 employees have stakeholder groups; micro-enterprises remain without such groups.
tactical_explanations:
Reciprocity is the core: expectations run in both directions.

The statement is true.

Stakeholder status does not end the business's counter-claims — for example to performance or payment.

The statement is false.

Several groups at once, not only a single stakeholder relationship.

The statement is true.

Stakeholder groups and stakeholders denote the same matter.

The statement is true.

Small businesses also have stakeholders. Size is not a prerequisite.

The statement is false.

title: Small enterprises in the size table
context: Assess the following statements on the category of small enterprises:
statements: Small enterprises have up to 49 employees and turnover or balance-sheet total of up to 10 million euros.
A business with 8 employees and 5 million euros of annual turnover remains a micro-enterprise.
Micro-enterprises and small enterprises share the same threshold values in the EU table.
A business with 40 employees as well as 8 million euros of turnover lies within the thresholds of small enterprises.
Micro and small enterprises differ financially: up to 2 million euros versus up to 10 million euros for turnover or balance-sheet total.
tactical_explanations:
Small class: up to 49 persons and up to 10 million euros turnover or balance-sheet total.

The statement is true.

5 million euros of turnover breaks the micro limit of 2 million euros — despite a low headcount.

The statement is false.

The thresholds differ clearly (2 vs. 10 million; 9 vs. 49 persons).

The statement is false.

40 and 8 million lie under the small thresholds.

The statement is true.

2 million vs. 10 million: that is the financial difference between the two rows.

The statement is true.

title: SMEs in the EU and turnover under one million
context: Assess the following statements on SME shares and on the turnover distribution of the number of enterprises:
statements: Around 99 percent of enterprises in the EU are SMEs.
Approximately 85 percent of enterprises have less than one million euros of turnover.
From the 85 percent figure it follows that these businesses lie above the micro threshold of 2 million euros of annual turnover.
The share of around 99 percent SMEs means that there are practically no large enterprises in the EU.
SME comprises micro, small and medium-sized enterprises below the class of large ones.
tactical_explanations:
EU-wide, the SME count dominates at around 99 percent.

The statement is true.

Under one million euros of turnover lie about 85 percent of businesses — still under the micro turnover threshold of 2 million.

The statement is true.

Under 1 million lies under 2 million — thus within, not above, the micro threshold.

The statement is false.

99 percent SMEs leaves around 1 percent large enterprises. "No large enterprises" does not follow from that.

The statement is false.

Three subclasses below the large ones: that is the SME collective term.

The statement is true.

title: High-turnover large enterprises in Austria
context: Assess the following statements on Austria's highest-turnover enterprises:
statements: Among Austria's highest-turnover enterprises are, for example, OMV AG, Porsche Holding GmbH and Strabag SE.
This ranking measures size by turnover, not by mere brand awareness.
Because SMEs dominate by number, high-turnover large enterprises cannot occur in Austria.
REWE International AG, Spar, voestalpine AG, Mondi AG, ÖBB AG, Andritz AG and Red Bull GmbH also belong among the high-turnover examples.
Whoever stands in this turnover peak falls under micro-enterprises according to the EU table.
tactical_explanations:
The named groups stand as examples of the turnover peak.

The statement is true.

The yardstick is turnover, not popularity of the brand.

The statement is true.

Many small businesses and a few high-turnover large ones do not rule each other out.

The statement is false.

Further high-turnover names complement the same top group.

The statement is true.

Turnover peak and micro class contradict each other. These groups are large enterprises.

The statement is false.

title: Demand, costs and profit intent
context: Assess the following statements on the relationship of receipts, expenditures and profit intent:
statements: Strong customer demand alone does not guarantee a profit if those expenditures exceed the receipts.
woom and Manner are run with profit intent, even though they would not legally have to be in order to count as enterprises.
The usual guideline of profit-oriented businesses is solely bare cost coverage without any surplus.
Profits can be reinvested and thus support performance and competitiveness.
In accounting terms, profit means steering revenues and expenses so that they balance each other as exactly as possible.
tactical_explanations:
Demand without cost coverage yields a loss. Profit needs a surplus of receipts.

The statement is true.

Profit intent is usual, but legally not a prerequisite for the concept of an enterprise.

The statement is true.

Profit orientation aims at a surplus, not only at a zero result. Bare cost coverage is more an NPO guideline.

The statement is false.

Reinvestment keeps businesses competitive.

The statement is true.

Equality of revenues and expenses is cost coverage, not profit. Profit means revenues above expenses.

The statement is false.

title: NPO between cost coverage and surplus
context: An advisory institution run as a non-profit organisation accepts donations and occasionally ploughs surpluses back into the offer. Assess the following statements:
statements: An NPO's primary orientation remains cost coverage, even when surpluses flow back into the offer.
Donation funds are an example of receipts with which goals can be pursued better.
Without adequate receipts an NPO still pursues its goals just as well, because non-profit makes financing superfluous.
Reinvested surpluses can improve the offer without profit maximisation following as the purpose.
Every accounting surplus legally transforms the NPO into an enterprise that must be oriented toward making a profit.
tactical_explanations:
Cost coverage remains the primary goal; ploughing surpluses back does not automatically change the purpose.

The statement is true.

Donations are typical NPO receipts for pursuing goals.

The statement is true.

Without means, the work stalls. Non-profit does not mean free of financing.

The statement is false.

Reinvestment strengthens the offer without making profit maximisation the purpose.

The statement is true.

A surplus alone does not force a profit orientation. Legally, NPOs can be enterprises without a profit compulsion.

The statement is false.

title: Several sectors, energy and crafts
context: Assess the following statements on sector assignment beyond the three core examples:
statements: Whether a business operates in one or several economic sectors depends on the object of the enterprise.
The energy industry counts toward the secondary sector.
Crafts belong, together with industry, to the secondary sector.
The energy industry counts toward the primary sector because electricity comes from natural resources.
An enterprise cannot operate in more than one economic sector at the same time.
tactical_explanations:
The object decides single- or multi-sector activity.

The statement is true.

Energy belongs to the secondary assignment alongside industry and crafts.

The statement is true.

Crafts produce and process — secondary, not tertiary or primary.

The statement is true.

Resource origin does not make energy primary production. Primary is extraction; secondary is processing/energy.

The statement is false.

Several sectors at once are possible if the object supports that.

The statement is false.

title: Forestry, fisheries, construction and craft trades
context: Assess the following statements on finer assignments in sectors and industries:
statements: Forestry as well as fisheries belong to the raw-material extraction of the primary sector.
The erection of buildings illustrates that construction industry.
Joinery shops, plumbers, electricians as well as locksmiths concretise crafts as an industry.
Wholesale and retail trade are forms of the trade industry.
Hospitality counts toward mining and thus toward the primary sector.
tactical_explanations:
Forestry and fisheries are primary production — primary.

The statement is true.

Building erection is the core example of construction.

The statement is true.

The named trades stand for craft industries.

The statement is true.

Trade subdivides among other things into wholesale and retail.

The statement is true.

Hospitality is a service (tertiary), not mining.

The statement is false.

title: Size, sector and location claims
context: Assess the following statements that link size classes, sectors and stakeholder groups:
statements: The numerical dominance of SMEs does not rule out that high-turnover businesses such as voestalpine AG help shape the secondary sector.
Because the tertiary sector contributes around 70 percent of economic output in Austria, steel production is to be assigned to the tertiary sector.
The location municipality expects jobs as well as levies together with meeting obligations, environmental care and social responsibility.
Micro-enterprises under the EU table and Austria's highest-turnover groups fall into the same size class.
An enterprise can be assigned to several industries, while that sector affiliation follows the object of the enterprise.
tactical_explanations:
Many small ones and a few large ones can shape the same sector — count and turnover effect diverge.

The statement is true.

Sector follows the object. Steel production is secondary, no matter how large the tertiary national share is.

The statement is false.

Location expectations bundle economic and societal points.

The statement is true.

Micro and turnover peak are opposite classes.

The statement is false.

Multiple industry assignment is possible; sector follows the object.

The statement is true.

title: Enterprise size under the EU recommendation
context: A management consultant assigns businesses to size classes under the EU recommendation. Assess the following statements on enterprise size:
statements: A bicycle shop with 9 employees, 1.8 million euros turnover and 1.6 million euros balance-sheet total counts as a micro-enterprise.

A supplier with 45 employees, 9 million euros turnover and 11 million euros balance-sheet total still counts among small enterprises, because for turnover and balance-sheet total one of the two limits is enough.
A mechanical-engineering business with 240 employees and 65 million euros turnover remains medium-sized, because the headcount under 250 alone decides.
A business with 200 employees, 55 million euros turnover and 40 million euros balance-sheet total remains medium-sized, because the balance-sheet total lies under 43 million euros.
For medium-sized enterprises the balance-sheet total upper limit of 50 million euros lies above the turnover upper limit of 43 million euros.
tactical_explanations:
All three micro thresholds are met.

The statement is true.

Turnover under 10 million is enough despite balance-sheet total over 10 million for the small financial limit (OR logic).

The statement is true.

65 million turnover breaks the medium turnover limit of 50 million — headcount alone does not save the medium class.

The statement is false.

For the medium class one of the two financial limits is enough; balance-sheet total under 43 million holds the class even though turnover lies over 50 million.

The statement is true.

The reverse is correct: turnover up to 50 million, balance-sheet total up to 43 million euros.

The statement is false.

title: EU size classes: pitfalls with OR/AND
context: Four businesses are to be assigned to the EU size classes. The thresholds themselves are not printed. Assess the following statements:
statements: A business with 8 employees, 1.5 million euros turnover and 2.3 million euros balance-sheet total remains a micro-enterprise, because at least the turnover lies under 2 million euros.
A business with 40 employees and 9 million euros turnover is automatically a small enterprise regardless of the balance-sheet total.
A business with 9 employees as well as 12 million euros turnover remains a micro-enterprise, because the headcount lies under 10.
A business with 249 employees, 50 million euros turnover as well as 43 million euros balance-sheet total still lies in the medium category.
A business with 250 employees as well as only 20 million euros turnover already counts among large enterprises.
tactical_explanations:
OR for the financial limits: turnover under 2 million holds the micro class despite a higher balance-sheet total.

The statement is true.

Without looking at the balance-sheet total a criterion is missing. If it exceeds 10 million, the small assignment no longer applies.

The statement is false.

12 million turnover breaks micro and also the small turnover limit — headcount alone is not enough.

The statement is false.

249 / 50 / 43 lie exactly at the upper medium limits and still count toward the medium category.

The statement is true.

From 250 employees the large class is reached — regardless of the lower turnover.

The statement is true.

title: FunBike: size class from memory
context: At year-end FunBike GmbH reports a balance-sheet total of 9,638,250 euros. Further threshold values are not repeated here. Assess the following statements on the EU size class and the SME concept:
statements: Solely because of a balance-sheet total of around 9.6 million euros, FunBike can still fall under small enterprises, provided headcount and turnover meet the remaining limits.
Solely because of this balance-sheet total, that micro-enterprise category is ruled out.
Solely because that balance-sheet total lies under the balance-sheet total limit of medium-sized enterprises, FunBike is automatically a large enterprise.
Around 99 percent of enterprises in the EU count among micro, small as well as medium-sized enterprises.
Large enterprises also belong to SMEs under the SME concept, because they form that largest of the four size classes.
tactical_explanations:
Under 10 million balance-sheet total the small financial limit remains open; the remaining criteria must fit.

The statement is true.

Over 2 million balance-sheet total rules out micro.

The statement is true.

Lying under the medium balance-sheet total limit makes no one a large enterprise.

The statement is false.

SME = the three classes below the large ones; around 99 percent.

The statement is true.

SME precisely excludes large enterprises.

The statement is false.

title: Austria's enterprise landscape in shares
context: Assess the following statements on the Austrian enterprise landscape and the importance of SMEs:
statements: In Austria too, SMEs dominate with around a 99 percent share of the number of enterprises.
Because around 90 percent of enterprises have fewer than ten employees, around 90 percent of all employed persons also work in such micro businesses.
Approximately 85 percent of enterprises have less than one million euros of turnover per year.
Around two thirds of employed persons work in SMEs.
Around 1,900 large enterprises make up only a small part of the number of enterprises and therefore also generate only around 10 percent of total turnover.
tactical_explanations:
Austria mirrors the EU dominance of the SME count.

The statement is true.

Number of enterprises and employment share are not identical. Far fewer than 90 percent of employed persons work in micro businesses.

The statement is false.

The 85 percent figure refers to the number of enterprises under 1 million euros of turnover.

The statement is true.

Employment focus of SMEs: around two thirds.

The statement is true.

A few large enterprises account for a little more than one third of turnover — not only around 10 percent.

The statement is false.

title: EU size classes: interplay of the criteria
context: Assess the following statements on the interplay of headcount, turnover and balance-sheet total in the EU size classification of enterprises:
statements: For an enterprise to be assigned to a size class, turnover as well as balance-sheet total must simultaneously undershoot the same euro limit; one criterion alone is not enough.
For medium-sized enterprises the turnover and balance-sheet total limits lie at 50 and 43 million euros respectively.
Whoever has 250 employees is a large enterprise regardless of turnover and balance-sheet total.

An enterprise with 30 employees and 3 million euros of turnover counts automatically among small enterprises solely because of the headcount under 49, even if turnover and balance-sheet total exceed the large limits.
Small and micro-enterprises each have the same euro limit for turnover and balance-sheet total (2 and 10 million euros respectively).
tactical_explanations:
For the financial criteria an OR logic applies: one of the two limits is enough.

The statement is false.

50 million turnover, 43 million balance-sheet total: those are the differing medium limits.

The statement is true.

The headcount threshold of 250 alone decides the large class.

The statement is true.

Financial limits can pull the class upward; headcount alone does not fix a small assignment.

The statement is false.

Micro: 2 million; small: 10 million — each the same for turnover and balance-sheet total.

The statement is true.

title: EU size classes: threshold values from memory
context: Assess the following statements on the threshold values of the EU size classification. An overview table is not provided:
statements: Micro-enterprises may have up to 49 employees as long as turnover or balance-sheet total do not exceed 2 million euros.
The turnover limit of small enterprises lies at 10 million euros, not at 50 million euros.
A business with exactly 249 employees still lies in the medium category; with exactly 250 it already lies in the large one.
A business with a balance-sheet total of exactly 43 million euros already counts among large enterprises for that reason alone.
A business with 10 employees is no longer a micro-enterprise by headcount, even if turnover as well as balance-sheet total remain low.
tactical_explanations:
Micro ends at 9 employees. 49 is the headcount threshold of small enterprises.

The statement is false.

10 million is the small turnover limit; 50 million belongs to the medium class.

The statement is true.

The boundary between medium and large lies between 249 and 250 employees.

The statement is true.

43 million balance-sheet total is the upper medium limit — large class does not follow from that alone.

The statement is false.

From 10 employees the micro headcount threshold is exceeded.

The statement is true.

title: Importance of the legal form
context: Evaluate the following statements on the legal form of enterprises:
statements: The legal form is important for the question of who manages the enterprise, who runs the business, and who is liable for debts.
For the choice of legal form, the industry is what mainly matters; how the capital is to be raised plays only a secondary role.
Most enterprises in Austria are SMEs, the majority of which are Einzelunternehmen.
Anyone who starts on a small scale with savings typically chooses the same legal form as a capital-intensive industrial business.
Anyone who does business with an enterprise should be clear about who is allowed to conclude contracts for the enterprise.
tactical_explanations:
Management, running the business, and liability are not side issues. Legal rules attach precisely to the idea that business partners should know who manages, who runs the business, who may conclude contracts, who has contributed capital, and who stands for the debts. The legal form answers exactly this bundle of questions, not merely the company name on letterhead. Without that assignment it would remain unclear whether a signature binds and whose private assets are at stake when invoices go unpaid. Treating the legal form as a mere label misses why it matters for all of these points and why interested parties look it up in the Firmenbuch if the enterprise is registered.

The statement is true.

Raising capital and liability are among the central criteria when choosing a legal form — not only the industry.

The statement is false.

SMEs and Einzelunternehmen dominate the landscape. Most enterprises in Austria are SMEs, and the majority of those are organised as Einzelunternehmen. Large enterprises with high capital needs often choose other forms, but that does not change the frequency: the typical Austrian business is small and often an Einzelunternehmen. The statement captures exactly that weighting, without turning every SME into a well-capitalised large firm.

The statement is true.

Small start-ups and large industrial businesses have different capital and liability requirements; the same legal form is not the normal case.

The statement is false.

Authority to contract is part of the same clarity. Anyone who does business with enterprises should know who manages, who runs the business, who may conclude contracts, who has contributed capital, and who is liable. The legal form matters for all of these questions, including external representation. Without that assignment it would remain unclear whether a signature binds the enterprise. That is exactly why the legal rules on legal form exist.

The statement is true.

title: Einzelunternehmen and one person
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Einzelunternehmen:
statements: An Einzelunternehmen is characterised by the fact that only one person runs the enterprise, makes the decisions, and bears the entrepreneurial risk.
An Einzelunternehmen requires — like the Offene Gesellschaft — at least two partners.
Independence and freedom from other partners in managing the enterprise are set against the risk borne alone.
Two people who want to manage and be liable on equal terms thereby already form an Einzelunternehmen.
Many small enterprises are organised as Einzelunternehmen.
tactical_explanations:
One person combines management, decision-making, and risk. That is exactly what characterises the Einzelunternehmen: only one person runs it, makes the decisions, and bears the entrepreneurial risk. There is no second owner with whom management and liability would be shared. Reading several equal heads into this form misses the definition. Concentration on one person is the starting point, not a special case of small shops.

The statement is true.

The defining feature of the Einzelunternehmen is exactly one managing person. Two partners point to a partnership.

The statement is false.

Independence has a price. Independence and freedom from other partners in managing the enterprise always stand, in the theory, against the risk that the sole trader must bear alone in full. Nobody else needs to co-decide, and nobody shares unlimited liability with private assets. If the business fails, that often hits the person privately, up to personal insolvency. The statement holds exactly this contrast, instead of confusing independence with a risk-free position or silently limiting liability to shop inventory.

The statement is true.

Equal management breaks the form. The Einzelunternehmen knows only one person who manages, decides, and bears the risk. If two people want to share tasks, financing, and liability, the path in the theory is a partnership, for example the Offene Gesellschaft with at least two partners. That does not create an Einzelunternehmen. The number two is not a detail here but a change of legal form.

The statement is false.

Small and simple often go together. Many small enterprises are organised as Einzelunternehmen because they can be founded relatively easily and without minimum capital requirements. Frequency follows from this low threshold, not from a ban on other forms. The statement captures the typical choice named in the theory, without claiming every small enterprise must be organised this way.

The statement is true.

title: Unlimited liability in the Einzelunternehmen
context: A Viennese carpenter runs her trade as an Einzelunternehmen. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The sole trader is liable without limit for all debts, that is not only with business assets but also with private assets.
In practice the sole trader’s liability remains limited to machines, inventory, and the business account; private assets stay out of reach.
If the Einzelunternehmen fails, that often means not only the end of the business but also financial difficulties as a private person.
Failed self-employment is a common reason for personal insolvency.
As soon as the carpenter employs two journeymen, they are liable without limit in her place for the business debts.
tactical_explanations:
Business assets are not the outer limit. The sole trader is liable without limit for all debts of her enterprise, meaning liability is not only with business assets but also with private assets. Creditors can therefore reach beyond the workbench and stock to a home, savings, or other private assets, insofar as the law allows. The carpenter alone bears the entrepreneurial risk; staff do not change that. Limiting liability to the business circle describes limited liability, which the theory precisely does not attribute to the Einzelunternehmen.

The statement is true.

In an Einzelunternehmen unlimited liability also reaches private assets — business assets do not cap it.

The statement is false.

Business and person collapse together in failure. If the Einzelunternehmen ends, that often means not only the end for the enterprise but also financial difficulties for the entrepreneur as a private person, because liability includes private assets. The carpenter may close the shop and still face open loans and supplier claims as a private person. Exactly this link is what the theory describes, rather than treating failure as merely wiping out the firm with no private consequences.

The statement is true.

Personal insolvency is not a fringe phenomenon. Failed self-employment is a common reason for personal insolvency, that is a debt settlement procedure for private persons. That follows from unlimited liability: business debts become private over-indebtedness when the enterprise no longer carries them. The statement reflects that point without turning every failed business into automatic court proceedings; the link is frequent, not every case without exception.

The statement is true.

Journeymen are not liability carriers in place of the owner. Sometimes employees are hired for support, but unlimited liability remains with the sole trader. She manages, decides, and bears the risk; employment transfers neither management nor debt liability to the staff. Treating the journeymen as substitute debtors confuses an employment contract with ownership.

The statement is false.

title: Formation and capital of the Einzelunternehmen
context: Evaluate the following statements on formation and financing of the Einzelunternehmen:
statements: Many small enterprises are organised as Einzelunternehmen because they can be founded relatively easily and without minimum capital requirements.
For every Einzelunternehmen the law prescribes a minimum capital sum of 10,000 euros.
The capital needed must ordinarily be raised by the sole trader alone.
If own funds are not enough, the further need for financial means is in most cases covered by a loan.
An Einzelunternehmen may raise missing funds only through additional partners, not through credit.
tactical_explanations:
Simplicity and the absence of minimum capital explain the frequency. Many small enterprises choose the Einzelunternehmen because formation is relatively simple and there are no minimum capital requirements. The owner need not prove a legally fixed starting capital to use the form; the money needed is ordinarily raised alone, often from savings. If that is not enough, a loan usually follows, not a second partner. That eases entry on a small scale but leaves unlimited liability untouched. The statement links organisational form and formation threshold in the way they belong together.

The statement is true.

Minimum capital of 10,000 euros applies to the GmbH, not to the Einzelunternehmen.

The statement is false.

Raising it alone is the normal path. The capital needed must ordinarily be raised by the sole trader alone, because no further partners contribute capital. Savings and later earned funds carry the business. The wording “ordinarily” leaves room for exceptions but does not change the rule: the one person stands for the equity.

The statement is true.

Credit closes the gap, not a second owner. If own funds are not enough, the further need for financial means is in most cases covered by a loan. That is presented as the typical path without excluding other sources. Debt capital sits beside the equity raised alone; it does not turn the Einzelunternehmen into a company. The statement captures this common financing line.

The statement is true.

Credit is the usual way to cover missing own funds in an Einzelunternehmen.

The statement is false.

title: Staff and risk in the Einzelunternehmen
context: Evaluate the following statements on division of labour in the Einzelunternehmen:
statements: Often only the sole trader works for the enterprise.
Sometimes a few employees are hired for support.
Anyone who employs staff no longer bears the entrepreneurial risk personally, because the employees take over liability.
Independence in managing the enterprise typically stands against the risk that the individual largely bears alone.
Several equal owners can jointly run one and the same Einzelunternehmen as one person.
tactical_explanations:
Working alone is the common case. Often only the sole trader works for the enterprise; the form does not require a workforce. Management, decision-making, and risk then visibly lie with the same person. The statement describes this typical situation without ruling out employing staff. Small scale and doing the work oneself belong together in the theory.

The statement is true.

Support does not change the legal form. Sometimes a few employees are hired for support. They help in the business but do not become partners. The one person continues to manage, make the important decisions, and bear the entrepreneurial risk. Staff are help, not co-ownership.

The statement is true.

Employment does not shift liability. Employees support but are not unlimitedly liable in place of the owner. The sole trader alone bears the risk in full, even if two or three people stand in the shop. Unlimited liability with private assets remains with the owner. The statement wrongly turns an employment relationship into an assumption of liability.

The statement is false.

Independence and sole risk are a pair. Independence and freedom from other partners in managing the enterprise always stand against the risk that the individual must bear alone in full. Nobody else needs to co-decide, and nobody shares unlimited liability with private assets. Staff for support do not change this burden, because employees do not stand in for the owner for business debts. “Always” is the standard wording here, not exaggeration. Reading independence as a risk-free position separates what the business logic binds together.

The statement is true.

Several owners break the definition. The Einzelunternehmen is characterised by only one person managing, deciding, and bearing the risk. Equal joint ownership is the situation of a partnership with more than one person involved, not of an Einzelunternehmen. The fiction that several people are “one person” does not change the legal assignment.

The statement is false.

title: Partnerships at a glance
context: Evaluate the following statements on partnerships:
statements: More than one person is involved in a partnership.
The persons involved not only raise the capital; they are also liable for the debts of the enterprise.
Whether partners work in the enterprise depends on the type of participation.
A partnership already arises when a sole owner hires a few employees.
Among partnerships a distinction is drawn between the Offene Gesellschaft and the Kommanditgesellschaft.
tactical_explanations:
More than one person is the threshold. More than one person is involved in a partnership; that distinguishes it from the Einzelunternehmen with only one managing person. Two or more people raise capital and stand for debts. Headcount here is not a stylistic device but a defining feature. A sole owner does not meet this threshold.

The statement is true.

Capital and liability lie with the same participants. The persons not only raise the capital for the enterprise; they are also liable for the debts. Depending on the type of partner, liability reaches into private assets or, for a limited partner, up to the contribution. Work in the business may be added but is not the only contribution. The statement holds the double role: money and standing for debts.

The statement is true.

Work follows the partner type. Depending on which kind of partner is involved, the participants also work in the enterprise. In the Offene Gesellschaft all are entitled and obliged to manage; in the Kommanditgesellschaft the general partner works in a comparable way, while the limited partner does not, but has control rights and may inspect the books. Both forms raise capital and both bear liability, only to different extents. The blanket claim that all partnership partners always work would therefore be too coarse. The statement allows exactly this differentiation without making work a condition of every capital contribution.

The statement is true.

Employees do not make a partnership. The Einzelunternehmen remains an Einzelunternehmen even if a few employees are hired for support. A partnership requires more than one person involved, that is partners, not merely staff. Hiring does not turn the owner’s management, capital raising, and liability into a company. The statement confuses an employment contract with participation.

The statement is false.

Two variants structure the subject. Among partnerships a distinction is drawn between Offene Gesellschaft and Kommanditgesellschaft. The OG knows only one kind of partner; the KG distinguishes general partner and limited partner. Other forms are not treated here as partnerships. The statement reflects that classification.

The statement is true.

title: Offene Gesellschaft
context: Two consultants want to found an Offene Gesellschaft together. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The Offene Gesellschaft knows only one kind of partner.
At least two partners found the OG.
All partners of the OG are entitled and obliged to manage the business.
A single person can found an OG alone if she raises the share capital of 10,000 euros.
For the capital of the OG there is, as with the Einzelunternehmen, no statutory minimum amount.
tactical_explanations:
One kind of partner, not two classes. The Offene Gesellschaft knows only one kind of partner; all stand in the same role. There is no type with limited liability beside a fully liable type. Exactly that distinguishes the OG from the Kommanditgesellschaft with general partner and limited partner. The statement captures this uniformity.

The statement is true.

The number two is a formation requirement. At least two partners found the OG. One person alone does not meet that, regardless of capital. The two consultants’ plan therefore fits the form; one of them alone would have to choose an Einzelunternehmen or find a second participating person. The statement reflects the minimum number.

The statement is true.

Management is a right and duty of all. All partners of the OG are entitled and obliged to manage the business. Nobody may retreat into the role of a silent capital contributor who only gives money and does not manage; such a limit to capital without work describes the limited partner of the KG in the theory, not the OG. The two consultants would therefore both run the business, not only one of them as an employed manager. Entitlement without obligation or the reverse is not how the OG is described. Liability and management lie with the same kind of partner.

The statement is true.

The OG needs at least two partners and has no statutory minimum capital. 10,000 euros is the GmbH threshold.

The statement is false.

No statutory minimum amount, as with the Einzelunternehmen. Every partner participates in the capital, for which however, as with the Einzelunternehmen, there is no statutory minimum amount. The OG is therefore not tied to a prescribed starting sum. If own funds are lacking, a bank loan often remains, as with other partnerships. The statement links OG and Einzelunternehmen exactly at this point.

The statement is true.

title: Joint and several liability in the OG
context: Three partners jointly run an Offene Gesellschaft. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Every partner is liable with their entire private assets for the full amount of the enterprise’s debts.
In the OG each participating person is liable only proportionally up to the amount of their own capital contribution — similar to GmbH shareholders.
Joint and several liability in the OG means that creditors can claim the full amount of the debts from every partner.
Anyone in the OG who only handles purchasing is not liable for debts arising from sales.
All OG partners participate in the capital of the enterprise.
tactical_explanations:
Private assets and the full amount belong together. Every partner of the OG is liable with their entire private assets for the full amount of the enterprise’s debts; that is called joint and several liability. Creditors need not content themselves with one third per head if three people are involved. They can seek the whole open amount from one person, and private assets stand for that, not only the contribution. Limiting liability to the business share describes the limited partner, not the OG.

The statement is true.

OG partners are jointly and severally liable without limit with private assets for the full amount, not only up to the contribution.

The statement is false.

Joint and several means: each person stands for the full amount, not only for a fraction.

The statement is true.

Division of tasks does not dissolve liability. Partners may share tasks and focus on purchasing, sales, or advice; all OG partners remain entitled and obliged to manage and are jointly and severally liable for the full amount. Debts from sales are debts of the enterprise, not a private special account of the seller. Anyone who only handles purchasing still stands outwardly for the whole amount.

The statement is false.

Capital participation belongs to the role. Every partner participates in the capital of the enterprise; there is no statutory minimum amount. The OG knows no class that only manages and gives no capital, and no class that only gives money and does not manage. Participation in capital and joint and several liability run in parallel. The statement holds this capital contribution.

The statement is true.

title: Kommanditgesellschaft: two kinds of partner
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Kommanditgesellschaft:
statements: The Kommanditgesellschaft distinguishes between general partners (Komplementäre) and limited partners (Kommanditisten).
At least one person is a general partner, and beside that there is at least one person as limited partner.
The general partner is comparable to an OG partner with regard to work in the business, capital participation, and liability.
All partners of a KG are equally liable only with their capital contribution, comparable to the GmbH.
The KG, like the OG, knows only a single kind of partner.
tactical_explanations:
Two types carry the KG. The Kommanditgesellschaft distinguishes between two kinds of partner, general partners and limited partners. That is the contrast to the OG, which knows only one kind. Liability, work, and capital follow from this distinction: the general partner resembles the OG partner; the limited partner is liable only with the contribution and does not work in the business. A uniform status for all participants would abolish this split. The statement names exactly that distinction without yet spelling out the minimum numbers.

The statement is true.

At least one person of each type. At least one person is a general partner; beside that there is still at least one person as limited partner. If either role is missing, the KG described is incomplete. Two general partners without a limited partner would be something other than this form; a sole limited partner without a general partner likewise. The minimum numbers stand that way.

The statement is true.

The general partner mirrors the OG role. With regard to work in the enterprise, participation in capital, and liability, the general partner is comparable to an OG partner. He works in the business, may contribute capital, and is liable without limit with private assets for the full amount of the debts, not only with a contribution. The KG places the liability limitation with the other type, the limited partner, who is liable only with the contribution and does not work in the business. Reading the general partner as limitedly liable misses the comparison and turns two kinds of partner into one.

The statement is true.

Only limited partners are limited to the contribution; general partners are liable without limit like OG partners.

The statement is false.

A single kind describes the OG, not the KG. The Offene Gesellschaft knows only one kind of partner; the Kommanditgesellschaft distinguishes general partner and limited partner. Melting the KG into one class takes away the feature the theory puts at the start. The statement is therefore false.

The statement is false.

title: Limited partner: contribution, work, control
context: A limited partner contributes capital to a KG and does not work in the business. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The limited partner is liable only with her own capital contribution.
The limited partner does not work in the enterprise.
For this type of partner a limitation of liability is possible.
Limited partners have control rights and may inspect the books of the company.
The limited partner runs the business of the KG jointly with the general partner and is equally obliged to do so.
tactical_explanations:
The contribution is the liability limit of this type. At least one person as limited partner is liable only with her own capital contribution, not with entire private assets for the full amount of the debts. That distinguishes her from the general partner, who stands without limit like an OG partner, and from the sole trader, whose liability likewise reaches private assets. Creditors can generally seek from the limited partner only the capital contributed. For this type of partner the liability limitation is possible; it does not disappear because the KG also needs a fully liable general partner. The statement reflects this limitation.

The statement is true.

No work in the business is part of the role definition. The limited partner is presented as a person who is liable only with her own capital contribution and does not work in the enterprise. Management lies with the general partner. The limited partner in the scenario, who gives capital and does not work in the business, matches exactly this type. Making her a co-manager mixes the two kinds.

The statement is true.

Limitation of liability sits with this type. For the partner type limited partner a limitation of liability is possible, namely to the own capital contribution. For the general partner and the OG partner the theory does not provide this limitation. The KG exists precisely to take capital from people who do not want to stand without limit with private assets for the full amount. The statement captures this possibility without extending it to the general partner.

The statement is true.

Control replaces management but does not erase it as a right to information. Limited partners have control rights and may inspect the books of the company. They do not run the business but are not left without information. Inspection of the books is the counterpart to the absence of day-to-day work: anyone who does not manage daily should be able to check what happens with the capital invested. The statement names exactly these rights.

The statement is true.

Management lies with the general partner. Limited partners are not obliged to manage the business.

The statement is false.

title: From Einzelunternehmen to partnership
context: A growing Einzelunternehmen hits the limits of one person. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Einzelunternehmen whose scale grows so much that management or financing becomes too much for one person can be converted into partnerships.
Such a conversion can improve financing options and the liability situation and share responsibility for managing the enterprise.
The legal form of an Einzelunternehmen is fixed and cannot be transferred into a partnership even with strong growth.
After conversion into a partnership, practically only one person remains entitled to manage the business.
More than one person is involved in the partnership that then arises.
tactical_explanations:
Growth can break the form. If the scale of the enterprise increases markedly so that management and/or financing become too much for one person, Einzelunternehmen can be converted into partnerships. The sole owner brings in further participating persons instead of continuing alone. The statement describes exactly this transition provided for in the theory, not a ban on growing.

The statement is true.

Three motives name the business logic. Conversion is done to improve financing options and the liability situation and to share responsibility for managing the enterprise. Further people can contribute capital, bear liability, and manage when management or financing has become too much for one person. That improves the position relative to the sole risk of the Einzelunternehmen, without automatically creating limited liability for everyone: in the OG liability remains joint and several and unlimited; in the KG it is limited only for the limited partner. The statement captures the named goals without yet fixing the choice between OG and KG.

The statement is true.

Einzelunternehmen can be converted into partnerships when their scale grows.

The statement is false.

Partnerships distribute management among several partners or general partners.

The statement is false.

More than one person is the definition after the change. More than one person is involved in a partnership; exactly for that reason management, financing, and liability can rest on several shoulders. Conversion consists in turning the sole owner into a company with further participants. The statement follows directly from the definition.

The statement is true.

title: Capital and bank credit in partnerships
context: Evaluate the following statements on financing partnerships:
