statements: Partnerships are as a rule limited with regard to the funds contributed by the partners, because they usually have only a few partners.
These few partners are in many cases unable to contribute large sums of capital.
Partnerships are therefore also often dependent on financing through bank loans.
Because several people contribute capital, the need for bank loans disappears in practice for partnerships.
For the Einzelunternehmen as well, missing own capital is in most cases covered by a loan.
tactical_explanations:
Few heads limit the contributions. Partnerships are as a rule limited with regard to the funds contributed by the partners, because they usually have only a few partners. OG and KG are not forms with a large number of capital providers. The limitation follows from the number of persons, not from a statutory ban on high contributions. The statement reflects this rule.

The statement is true.

Large sums often lie beyond reach. The few partners are in many cases unable to contribute large sums of capital to the enterprise. The savings of two or three people often do not suffice for machine parks and large capacities, and a statutory minimum amount does not force them into large starting capital either. Exactly for that reason dependence on bank loans is named in the next step. The statement is the reason for this tightness, not yet the claim that credit is forbidden or superfluous. Partnerships thus typically remain thinner at the capital base than forms with many capital providers that this topic does not cover.

The statement is true.

Bank credit is the frequent supplement. Because the funds contributed remain limited, partnerships are therefore also often dependent on financing through bank loans. Partners’ equity and credit stand side by side; credit does not replace the legal form. “Often” is the nuance, not an absolute must. The statement captures this dependence.

The statement is true.

Few partners often cannot raise large sums; bank loans frequently remain necessary.

The statement is false.

Credit is already the typical add-on for the Einzelunternehmen. If own funds are not enough, the further need is in most cases covered by a loan. Partnerships stand in a similar financing line, only that several people contribute equity and often still need the bank. The statement connects both forms through the same debt-financing path.

The statement is true.

title: Who is liable and to what extent
context: Compare liability in the Einzelunternehmen, the OG, and the KG. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The sole trader is personally and unlimitedly liable, that is also with private assets.
OG partners are personally and unlimitedly liable, and each for the full amount of the debts.
The general partner is liable like the OG partner.
The limited partner is liable only up to the amount of his contribution.
The limited partner is liable with his entire private assets for the full amount of all debts, exactly like the general partner.
tactical_explanations:
One person, full liability. The sole trader is liable without limit for all debts, not only with business assets but also with private assets. Personal here means: the natural person stands for it, not only a ring-fenced business circle. Failure can lead to personal insolvency. The statement summarises exactly this unlimited personal liability.

The statement is true.

Joint and several and unlimited in the OG. Every partner is liable with entire private assets for the full amount of the debts; that is called joint and several liability. Personally and unlimitedly the position remains like the Einzelunternehmen, sharpened by the fact that each person stands for the whole amount, not only for their capital share. Three partners mean three full liability shoulders outwardly; creditors need not content themselves with thirds. The capital contribution is participation, not a cap. The statement matches overview and text and distinguishes the OG from the limited partner, who is liable only up to the contribution.

The statement is true.

General partner equals OG partner. With regard to work, capital participation, and liability the general partner is comparable to an OG partner; the summary expressly says the general partner is liable like the OG partner. Unlimited, personal, private assets, full amount: that applies to him, not to the limited partner. The KG splits the roles but does not abolish the full liability of the general partner.

The statement is true.

The contribution is the upper limit for the limited partner. The limited partner is liable only with his own capital contribution — in the overview: only up to the amount of his contribution. For this type a limitation of liability is possible. Private assets for the full amount are not required of him by the theory. Equating him with the general partner erases the point of the second kind of partner.

The statement is true.

Equating with the general partner is the error. Unlimited liability with entire private assets for the full amount describes OG partners and the general partner. The limited partner is liable only up to the amount of his contribution and does not work in the enterprise. The KG exists precisely because this limitation is meant to be possible. The statement assigns the wrong liability to the wrong type.

The statement is false.

title: Who runs the business
context: Evaluate the following statements on management in the Einzelunternehmen, OG, and KG:
statements: In the Einzelunternehmen the sole trader runs the business.
In the OG the OG partners run the business, at least two persons.
In the KG the general partner or general partners run the business, at least one person.
In the KG the limited partner runs the business, while the general partner does not work in it.
All partners of a KG are entitled and obliged to manage the business, exactly as in the OG.
tactical_explanations:
One person manages. The Einzelunternehmen is characterised by only one person running the enterprise and making the decisions. The summary names the sole trader as the one who runs the business. Employees may support but do not replace this management. The statement captures the assignment.

The statement is true.

At least two manage in the OG. All partners are entitled and obliged to manage; the OG is founded by at least two persons. The summary says: the OG partners, at least two, run the business. A sole managing owner would again be the Einzelunternehmen, even if she employs staff. Capital without a second person does not make an OG. The statement links headcount and management right as text and overview do.

The statement is true.

General partners lead the KG. The general partner is comparable to an OG partner with regard to work in the enterprise; the overview assigns management to the general partner or partners, at least one. The limited partner does not work in the business. At least one fully liable person who works in the business therefore carries the management. The statement follows text and overview.

The statement is true.

The roles stand reversed. The limited partner does not work in the enterprise and does not run the business; the general partner does both in the way comparable to the OG partner. Control rights and inspection of the books replace management for the limited partner; they are not themselves management. The statement swaps the two kinds and is false.

The statement is false.

The OG rule does not apply to all KG participants. Entitled and obliged to manage in the OG are all partners, because the OG knows only one kind. In the KG the same management role applies to the general partner, who works like an OG partner; the limited partner does not work in the enterprise and instead has control rights including inspection of the books. Treating all as in the OG would make the limited partner a manager and mix that type’s liability limitation with a management role the theory does not attribute to him. The two kinds of the KG would then again be one. The statement is false.

The statement is false.

title: Raising capital without a statutory minimum
context: Evaluate the following statements on raising capital in the Einzelunternehmen, OG, and KG:
statements: In the Einzelunternehmen the sole trader raises the capital.
In the OG the OG partners raise the capital.
In the KG the limited partner must make a capital contribution; the general partner may make a capital contribution.
For the Einzelunternehmen, OG, and KG there is in each case a statutory minimum capital sum as a formation requirement.
Additional equity can be raised by the limited partner by increasing his capital contribution.
tactical_explanations:
One person stands for the capital. The capital needed must ordinarily be raised by the sole trader alone; the overview says the same: the sole trader raises the capital. There are no further partners. If money is lacking, a loan follows in most cases, not a statutory minimum contribution. The statement captures the capital source.

The statement is true.

All OG participants take part in the capital. Every partner of the OG participates in the capital; the overview assigns capital raising to the OG partners. A statutory minimum amount is missing, as with the Einzelunternehmen. Management and capital contribution lie with the same kind of partner. The statement is correct.

The statement is true.

May and must distinguish the KG. The summary holds: the general partner may, the limited partner must make a capital contribution. The general partner remains comparable to the OG partner on liability and work; his contribution is possible but not formulated as a must in the same way as for the limited partner, whose role is precisely giving capital with limited liability and without working in the business. Additional equity is later raised by the limited partner by increasing the contribution, not by management. The statement reflects this asymmetry without turning the general partner into someone with only limited liability.

The statement is true.

No statutory minimum amount for these three forms. Einzelunternehmen can be founded without minimum capital requirements; for the capital of the OG there is, as with the Einzelunternehmen, no statutory minimum amount; for the KG the overview likewise names no minimum capital. A formation barrier through a prescribed sum does not belong to this set of person-based forms. The statement invents a threshold that the business logic denies here.

The statement is false.

An increased contribution is the limited partner’s path. Additional equity is raised by the limited partner by increasing the capital contribution; for the general partner the overview points to the same path as in the OG, that is further contributions by the partners. New large capital markets are not described for partnerships; few participants remain the rule. The statement captures the intended increase.

The statement is true.

title: Liability, formation, and management compared
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Einzelunternehmen, Offene Gesellschaft, and Kommanditgesellschaft:
statements: The OG partner is liable only with the business contribution; her private assets remain as a rule protected from creditors.
At least two persons found the Offene Gesellschaft; one person alone is not enough.
The limited partner is liable without limit with entire private assets for the full amount of the debts.
The general partner is comparable to an OG partner with regard to work, capital participation, and liability.
For the capital of Einzelunternehmen and OG there is no statutory minimum amount.
tactical_explanations:
Private assets are not protected in the OG. Every partner is liable with entire private assets for the full amount of the debts, jointly and severally. The business contribution is participation in capital, not the upper limit of liability; there is no statutory minimum amount, and missing minimum capital certainly does not mean creditor protection. Permanently protected private assets would be the logic of a liability limitation that the theory attributes to the limited partner, not to the OG and not to the Einzelunternehmen. Creditors can seek the whole amount from one partner. The statement confuses OG and limited contribution liability.

The statement is false.

The number two is mandatory. At least two partners found the OG; the form knows only this one kind of participant, but not sole formation. A person who manages, decides, and alone is liable remains a sole trader, even with the same turnover. Capital amount does not replace the second person, especially as there is no statutory minimum amount. The statement holds the formation threshold.

The statement is true.

Unlimited full liability is borne by the general partner. The limited partner is liable only with his own capital contribution, does not work in the business, and has control rights including inspection of the books. Standing without limit with entire private assets for the full amount is what OG partners, sole traders, and general partners do. The KG precisely splits this burden from the capital-providing type. Making the limited partner unlimitedly liable erases the liability limitation the theory attributes to this type.

The statement is false.

Three comparison axes name the business logic. With regard to work in the enterprise, participation in capital, and liability, the general partner is comparable to an OG partner. He manages along, may contribute capital, and is liable like the OG partner. The limited partner stands beside him with contribution, without work, with limited liability. The statement captures the general partner without turning the KG into an OG under another name.

The statement is true.

Both forms start without a statutory capital threshold. Einzelunternehmen are founded without minimum capital requirements; for the capital of the OG there is, as with the Einzelunternehmen, no statutory minimum amount. That eases entry but leaves unlimited liability untouched: missing minimum capital does not mean limited liability. Confusing the missing minimum with creditor protection mixes two different points. The statement itself on the minimum amount is correct.

The statement is true.

title: Idea of the capital company
context: Evaluate the following statements on capital companies:
statements: Higher capital sums can more readily be raised with capital companies.
Shareholders of a capital company must — as in the OG — themselves work in the enterprise and manage it.
The law provides a minimum capital amount for capital participation in a capital company.
Raising capital and management can be separated in capital companies.
Capital companies have no separate legal personality and are not regarded as legal persons.
tactical_explanations:
Many participants can pool larger amounts. The capital company stands beside the partnership precisely because higher capital sums can more readily be raised this way. The shareholders provide capital, are as a rule liable only with what they contributed, and need not themselves take on management. Exactly this combination makes it easier to attract many capital providers. Claiming that large sums are harder here than with a few personally liable persons reverses the logic.

The statement is true.

In capital companies, raising capital and management can be separated.

The statement is false.

Without a statutory lower limit this form does not work. It must be noted that the law provides a minimum capital amount for capital participation. That distinguishes the capital company from the Einzelunternehmen and from partnerships, for which no such statutory minimum amount applies. Share capital of the GmbH and stated capital of the AG are concrete expressions of this rule, not freely invented thresholds. Denying the minimum capital amount contradicts the core of capital participation in this form.

The statement is true.

Giving money and managing need not coincide in one person. Because shareholders are not necessarily entrusted with management, raising capital and management can be separated in capital companies. A shareholder can contribute capital and stay outside; a managing director can lead without being a shareholder. Exactly this separation is described as typical, not as a breach of the legal form.

The statement is true.

Capital companies are legal persons with their own legal personality.

The statement is false.

title: Legal person and acting
context: A Viennese software firm is founded as a GmbH. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: As a legal person the GmbH can do business, conclude contracts, sue, and be sued.
The capital company needs natural persons who act for it.
Only humans as natural persons may conclude contracts; the GmbH cannot do so in its own name.
Shareholders need not necessarily be entrusted with management.
Separate legal personality means that the GmbH can manage without a managing director.
tactical_explanations:
The GmbH itself stands in legal traffic. Capital companies are regarded as legal persons: they can do business, conclude contracts, sue, and be sued. Suppliers, customers, and courts deal with the company, not automatically with every private name behind the capital contributions. The software firm rents offices and buys licences as a GmbH. Natural persons must act for it; that does not change who holds the rights and duties. Exactly this capacity follows from separate legal personality, which the theory attributes to capital companies, in contrast to humans as natural persons.

The statement is true.

Without acting humans the shell stays silent. The legal person can hold rights, but it needs natural persons who act for it. Managing directors sign, negotiate, and represent. The company does not replace people; it needs them as organs.

The statement is true.

The contract does not hang on every shareholder’s private name. Precisely because the GmbH is a legal person, it concludes contracts in its own name. Natural persons act for it, but the obligation hits the company. The claim that only humans may conclude contracts and the GmbH cannot do so in its own name erases legal personality. Exactly the opposite stands in the theory.

The statement is false.

Capital providers need not manage day to day. Shareholders provide capital but are not necessarily entrusted with management. An employed managing director can lead the software firm without holding a capital contribution; a shareholder can contribute capital and leave management to others. Separation of raising capital and management is expressly possible in capital companies.

The statement is true.

Legal personality does not replace organs. The GmbH is managed by one or more managing directors; as a legal person it needs natural persons who act for it. Inferring from separate legal personality that no management organ is needed confuses the capacity to hold contracts with the capacity to act without humans. The shell alone does not sign.

The statement is false.

title: Share capital of the GmbH
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung:
statements: For a GmbH at least one shareholder must be present.
The share capital of a GmbH must by law amount to at least 10,000 euros.
Each capital contribution of a shareholder must amount to at least 70 euros.
A GmbH may only be founded with at least five shareholders — analogous to an AG with widely held shares.
At least half of the share capital must be raised in the form of money; the rest may also be a contribution in kind.
tactical_explanations:
One person suffices as the shareholder circle. Expressly: there must be at least one shareholder. The GmbH is therefore not a form that necessarily requires several heads. A founder can alone raise share capital and appoint a managing director, who may be herself or another person. Requiring five people for formation invents a threshold the law does not know.

The statement is true.

Ten thousand euros are the statutory lower limit of share capital. Since 1 January 2024 it amounts to at least 10,000 euros; before that it was 35,000 euros. Both figures are named; the current threshold is the lower one. Without this minimum amount the capital participation the law provides for the GmbH is missing. Treating the 10,000 euros as a non-binding tip misses the statutory rule.

The statement is true.

Seventy euros are the lower limit per contribution. Each capital contribution of a shareholder must amount to at least 70 euros. Several shareholders can therefore raise the share capital in pieces, but not in arbitrary cent amounts. The 70 euros stand beside the 10,000 euros of share capital; both thresholds belong to the GmbH, not to the AG. Below 70 euros per contribution the statutory minimum for the capital contribution would be missed.

The statement is true.

For the GmbH one shareholder suffices. Five are not a statutory minimum number.

The statement is false.

Cash and contribution in kind can share the load. At least half of the share capital must be raised in the form of money; the rest may also be a contribution in kind, for example a computer or a car. With 10,000 euros share capital at least 5,000 euros must therefore come as money; the remaining 5,000 euros may flow as assets in kind. Wanting the entire share capital exclusively in used equipment without the money share undershoots the half in money. Conversely the business logic expressly allows the rest not in cash but as assets in kind. Exactly this mix is what the sentence describes, not a free choice between only money or only assets without the half rule.

The statement is true.

title: Management of the GmbH
context: Two carpenters found a workshop GmbH and check who should manage and who should be liable. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The GmbH is managed by one or more managing directors.
The managing director must at the same time be a shareholder of the GmbH; external management is not permitted.
For management a salary is received; shareholders receive profit shares for their capital contributions.
GmbH shareholders are liable only with their capital contribution.
Additional equity in the GmbH can be raised only by issuing shares.
tactical_explanations:
Management lies with the management organ. The GmbH is managed by one or more managing directors. At least one person in this role is needed; several are permitted. The carpenters can appoint one of themselves or an external person. Without management there would be no natural person acting for the legal person. The statement captures exactly this organ rule, not the shareholders’ meeting of the AG.

The statement is true.

Management and shareholder status can fall apart; external managing directors are permitted.

The statement is false.

Salary and profit share are different channels. Whoever runs the business receives a salary for that. Whoever has contributed capital receives profit shares for the capital contribution. One person can be both and then receive both; they need not. Carpenters who only hold contributions and pay an external manager separate the two flows exactly as described. Mixing salary and profit share into one pot confuses organ remuneration and return on capital.

The statement is true.

The capital contribution limits liability. GmbH shareholders are liable only with their capital contribution, not without limit with private assets as in the Einzelunternehmen or for OG partners. Creditors of the workshop reach the company assets; the private house of a shareholder beyond that is not automatically available for liability. The carpenters risk the amount placed in the capital contribution if the legal person does not carry the debts. Exactly this limitation gives the form the name Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung. Drawing unlimited personal liability here describes the wrong legal form.

The statement is true.

Shares exist in the AG. In the GmbH, contributions or new shareholders increase equity.

The statement is false.

title: Liability in GmbH and AG
context: Evaluate the following statements on the liability of capital providers:
statements: Shareholders are not personally liable for the debts of the AG; they risk only the money they invest in buying shares.
Limited liability means that GmbH shareholders cannot lose the money put into the capital contribution.
GmbH shareholders are liable only with their capital contribution.
Because the stated capital is divided into shares, the members of the AG are called shareholders (Aktionäre).
Shareholders are liable without limit with their entire private assets for the full amount of the AG’s debts.
tactical_explanations:
Only the share purchase is at stake. Just as GmbH shareholders are not personally liable, Aktionäre are also not personally liable for the debts of the AG. They risk the money they invest in buying shares. If the AG becomes insolvent, they lose that stake; creditors cannot automatically reach every shareholder’s home and savings book. The overview says the same in other words: shareholders are liable only with their share capital. Personal, unlimited liability for the full amount of the debts belongs to OG partners, not to the AG. Equating both erases the point of the capital company.

The statement is true.

The capital contribution can be lost; what is limited is liability beyond that.

The statement is false.

Overview and running text name the same limit. GmbH shareholders are liable only with their capital contribution. That is the capital contribution they have made, not entire private assets. Creditors of the GmbH look to the assets of the legal person. The wording “only with their capital contribution” is the precise liability rule, not a loose paraphrase.

The statement is true.

The share turns the member into a shareholder. The capital that members contribute is called stated capital and is divided into shares; that is why the members are called Aktionäre. Anyone who has bought at least one share is a member of the AG. The name follows from the division of stated capital, not from the mere label member. Without that division there would be no shareholder status in the sense the theory uses.

The statement is true.

Shareholders risk only the share purchase price, not the rest of their private assets.

The statement is false.

title: Organs and stated capital of the AG
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Aktiengesellschaft:
statements: The stated capital of an AG must by law amount to at least 70,000 euros.
The stated capital is divided into shares.
The executive board runs the business on its own responsibility and represents the company.
The members of the executive board are appointed and dismissed by the supervisory board.
Large enterprises with high capital needs may not be organised as an AG, because the AG is intended only for small businesses.
tactical_explanations:
Seventy thousand euros are the lower limit of stated capital. The capital that members contribute is called stated capital and must by statutory rules amount to at least 70,000 euros. That lies clearly above the 10,000 euros share capital of the GmbH and below the 120,000 euros of the SE. Without this threshold the statutory capital participation of the AG is missing. Large enterprises with high capital needs often choose the form precisely because stated capital divided into shares can pool many capital providers. Treating 70,000 euros as a non-binding custom contradicts the statutory rule in the theory.

The statement is true.

Division creates the share. Because stated capital is divided into shares, the members are called Aktionäre. Each share is a portion of stated capital, not a loan. Additional equity can later be raised by issuing new shares that existing or new shareholders buy. Division is the defining feature, not an optional marketing label.

The statement is true.

Management and representation lie with the executive board. It runs the business on its own responsibility and represents the company. That is a different organ from the management of the GmbH, but fulfils the same practical role: natural persons act for the legal person. Own responsibility means the board manages, instead of every shareholder having to sign every contract personally. Exactly so the AG separates capital and management.

The statement is true.

Appointment comes from the supervisory board, not from every shareholder personally in daily life. The members of the executive board are appointed and dismissed by the supervisory board. The AG thus has a further organ between capital providers and management. Describing the board as purely self-appointed or as daily appointable and dismissable by every small shareholder skips the supervisory board. The statement reflects the rule.

The statement is true.

Precisely capital-intensive large enterprises are frequently organised as an AG.

The statement is false.

title: Flexible capital company
context: A start-up examines the FlexKapG as a form modelled on the GmbH. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Just as with the GmbH, one shareholder suffices for the FlexKapG.
The share capital of the FlexKapG is likewise 10,000 euros.
The minimum amount of a capital contribution in the FlexKapG is only 1 euro.
Enterprise-value participants have a claim to their profit share and at the same time have full voting rights like ordinary shareholders.
Enterprise-value shares are meant to enable simple participation by employees.
tactical_explanations:
One head suffices here too. The Flexible Kapitalgesellschaft is modelled on the GmbH: just as with the GmbH, one shareholder suffices. The start-up need not first gather a shareholder collective. The parallel to the GmbH concerns the shareholder circle, not automatically every detail of the capital contribution. Requiring two people to found a FlexKapG transfers the OG rule to the wrong form.

The statement is true.

Ten thousand euros also apply to the FlexKapG. Share capital is likewise 10,000 euros. The modelling on the GmbH includes this amount. What differs is mainly the minimal capital contribution and the figure of enterprise-value shares, not the share-capital sum itself. Assigning the AG stated capital of 70,000 euros to the FlexKapG mixes the forms.

The statement is true.

One euro replaces the seventy-euro threshold of the GmbH. The minimum amount of a capital contribution in the FlexKapG is only 1 euro; in the GmbH it is at least 70 euros. Small pieces ease finer participations. Share capital remains 10,000 euros; only the smallest permitted contribution falls. Demanding 70 euros for the FlexKapG as well ignores exactly this difference, which the theory names as essential beside enterprise-value shares.

The statement is true.

Enterprise-value participants receive profit shares but no voting rights.

The statement is false.

Employee participation is the purpose of the special form. A material difference from the GmbH is that the FlexKapG provides for enterprise-value shares, which are a special form of share capital and are meant to enable simple participation by employees. The start-up can let staff share in enterprise value without the same voting-rights cut as a full capital contribution: profit share yes, voting rights no. Share capital of 10,000 euros and the one-euro capital contribution remain beside that. The statement captures exactly this intent of simple participation, not a hidden renaming of classic GmbH shareholder status.

The statement is true.

title: European company
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Societas Europaea:
statements: The European company is also called Europäische Aktiengesellschaft or Societas Europaea (SE).
The legal framework for the SE is uniform and does not change with the EU or EEA member state in which the SE has its seat.
The minimum capital of the SE is 120,000 euros.
The SE is the prescribed legal form for every Austrian small trade without foreign connection.
Strabag, for example, is organised as an SE.
tactical_explanations:
Three names denote the same variant of the Aktiengesellschaft. The European company is also called Europäische Aktiengesellschaft or Societas Europaea (SE). It is a variant of the AG, not of the GmbH and not of the cooperative. The abbreviation SE appears with large, cross-border enterprises. Confusing the SE with the SCE, the European cooperative, reaches for the wrong Latin designation.

The statement is true.

Same framework regardless of seat state. The SE is a possible legal form for Aktiengesellschaften in the European Union and the European Economic Area. The legal framework is always the same, no matter in which EU or EEA member state the SE has its seat. Exactly that makes the form interesting for enterprises with establishments in several states, because they do not need a completely different company law shell in every country. The Strabag example logic fits: large, cross-border activity. Claiming that every seat country invents a completely different SE law contradicts this uniformity, which the theory names as an advantage.

The statement is true.

One hundred and twenty thousand euros are the threshold. Minimum capital is 120,000 euros, named in the overview beside the 70,000 euros of the AG. That lies above GmbH and national AG. Without this amount the statutory capital participation of the SE is missing. Using 10,000 or 70,000 euros as the SE minimum confuses the forms.

The statement is true.

The SE suits above all cross-border structures and is not prescribed for small trades without EU connection.

The statement is false.

Strabag shows the SE in practice. The enterprise is organised as a Societas Europaea and illustrates the European capital company in a large business with international connection. The form is not typical for a locally isolated small business without cross-border need. The example shows that the SE really occurs in Austria. Choice of legal form here follows size and international orientation.

The statement is true.

title: Purpose of the cooperative
context: Several nurseries want to use machines and buy jointly. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Cooperatives are associations of at least two natural and/or legal persons.
The aim is the promotion of the livelihood and the economy of their members.
In the foreground stands making profits, not joint economic activity.
Joint use of production plant and operating resources as well as joint purchasing and/or distribution are typical forms of joint economic activity.
The legal form in Austria is the registered cooperative (e. Gen.).
tactical_explanations:
Two are the lower limit; people and companies are admitted. Cooperatives are associations of at least two natural and/or legal persons. A single nursery alone is not yet a cooperative; GmbHs can be members beside persons. The number two distinguishes the form from the one-person GmbH. Founding a cooperative with only one member undershoots the rule.

The statement is true.

Member promotion is the purpose, not a side clause. The aim is the promotion of the livelihood and the economy of their members. The nurseries join so that each of them stands better economically, for example through shared machines or joint purchasing. The legal form serves the establishment of commercial and economic cooperatives. The motto “What one cannot achieve, many can” underlines the same point: joint scale instead of isolated profit maximisation of the shell. Narrowing the purpose to the profit of the legal person as an end in itself misses this orientation toward members that the theory puts first.

The statement is true.

Profit maximisation does not stand in front. In the foreground stands not making profits but joint economic activity. The motto is: What one cannot achieve, many can. Profits can be reinvested or paid out as rebates; they do not define the form. The statement turns foreground and background around and is false.

The statement is false.

Synergies arise through sharing and pooling. Joint use of production plant and operating resources and/or joint purchasing and/or distribution are the paths named in the theory. Jointly one reaches different scale. The nurseries can share a pond digger or order plants together. Exactly these examples carry the purpose of member promotion, without every cooperative having to take all three paths at once.

The statement is true.

e. Gen. is the Austrian designation. The legal form itself in Austria is the registered cooperative and serves the establishment of commercial and economic cooperatives. The European counterpart is the Societas Cooperativa Europaea (SCE). Confusing the Austrian form with the SE of Aktiengesellschaften reaches for the wrong European variant. The statement captures the national designation.

The statement is true.

title: Liability, vote, and organs of the cooperative
context: Evaluate the following statements on capital, liability, and decision-making in the cooperative:
statements: No minimum capital is necessary for the cooperative.
If a cooperative share is 100 euros, the member is ordinarily liable with a further 100 euros; the possible loss is at most 200 euros.
The highest organ of the cooperative is the general meeting.
Under one-person-one-vote each person has one vote regardless of their share of cooperative capital.
The articles of a cooperative may not usually replace one-person-one-vote with a diverging rule.
tactical_explanations:
No statutory capital threshold as with GmbH and AG. No minimum capital is necessary; members participate with a capital contribution. The overview repeats: minimum capital no. The nurseries need not pool 10,000 or 70,000 euros as a statutory lower limit. Imposing the GmbH’s share capital on the cooperative invents a threshold the theory expressly denies.

The statement is true.

Doubling is the worked example. Liability is ordinarily limited to a certain money amount. If a cooperative share is 100 euros, the member is liable with a further 100 euros; the possible loss is at most 200 euros. The overview says: with their contribution, as a rule in double amount. 100 plus 100 equals 200; that is the upper limit in the example, not unlimited personal liability with entire private assets as for OG partners. Equating a 100-euro share with unlimited access to house and account exceeds the rule. The sum remains 100 plus 100, not 100 plus everything.

The statement is true.

Management and highest organ do not coincide. Management is by the board, which is also formed from members. The highest organ, however, is the general meeting, in which the essential decisions are voted on. Declaring the board the highest instance skips the general meeting. The statement captures the ranking.

The statement is true.

One person, one vote, regardless of capital. One-person-one-vote means that in a vote each person has one vote regardless of their share of cooperative capital, and that vote is not weighted according to the capital share. Anyone holding 500 euros does not vote five times as heavily as anyone holding 100 euros, if the rule applies. That distinguishes the cooperative from a purely capital-weighted shareholders’ meeting.

The statement is true.

The articles can diverge. One-person-one-vote is named, with the addition that the articles of a cooperative can provide a diverging rule. “Never” closes exactly that opening. A cooperative may therefore weight differently in the articles; it need not. The absolute bar contradicts the text.

The statement is false.

title: Firmenbuch duty of capital companies
context: Evaluate the following statements on the Firmenbuch:
statements: GmbH, AG, and cooperatives must be entered in the Firmenbuch.
The Firmenbuch is a public, central court-run enterprise database that can be inspected.
Registration makes the enterprise more transparent, which can help business deals.
Capital companies may freely choose whether they enter the Firmenbuch, because only the Einzelunternehmen is subject to registration duty.
The Firmenbuch entry contains the firm name, the seat of the enterprise, and the object of the enterprise.
tactical_explanations:
Legal form decides the duty. The OG, KG, GmbH, and AG as well as cooperatives must be entered in the Firmenbuch. For this slice what counts above all is: GmbH, AG, and registered cooperative stand on the must-list, because essentially the legal form decides who must and who only may. Treating registration of the capital company as a hobby misses the duty. The Einzelunternehmen knows turnover thresholds and voluntary registration below them; that does not change the duty of the forms named here. Transparency toward business partners is the purpose, not an optional quality seal for GmbH and AG.

The statement is true.

Public, central, court-run. The Firmenbuch is a public, central court-run enterprise database that can be inspected. Business partners can look things up instead of following rumours. It is not a private club list. Exactly this description carries the transparency that the subject matter links to registration.

The statement is true.

Transparency is meant to ease deals. Through it the enterprise becomes more transparent, which can help business deals because partners can see important information on the enterprise in the Firmenbuch. Firm name, seat, object, and representation become visible. The statement reflects the purpose without claiming every contract comes about only after a Firmenbuch extract.

The statement is true.

Voluntariness does not apply to GmbH and AG. Some enterprises may, others must be registered; essentially the legal form decides. Capital companies and cooperatives must; the Einzelunternehmen only from a certain size, with voluntary registration below that. The claim that only the Einzelunternehmen is under duty and capital companies may choose reverses the rule.

The statement is false.

Name, place, and activity stand in the entry. The Firmenbuch entry contains the firm name, that is the legal name of the enterprise (for example woom GmbH), the seat, and the object of the enterprise. Further particulars are added, for example who may run the business. The statement names the core that the theory lists first and stays with that.

The statement is true.

title: What the Firmenbuch shows for GmbH and AG
context: A supplier looks up GmbH and AG in the Firmenbuch. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The names of the shareholders of a GmbH are apparent from the Firmenbuch entry.
The names of the shareholders of the AG are not contained in the Firmenbuch entry.
The amount of the capital contributions of GmbH shareholders is shown in the Firmenbuch.
The entry shows who may run the business.
Shareholders of an AG must stand by name in the Firmenbuch; GmbH shareholders by contrast usually need not.
tactical_explanations:
GmbH shareholders are visible by name. The entry contains the names of the shareholders, but not the Aktionäre of the AG. The supplier can see for a GmbH who holds capital contributions. That serves transparency toward business partners. Claiming that GmbH shareholders always remain anonymous in the Firmenbuch contradicts this list.

The statement is true.

Shareholder circles remain without a name list in the Firmenbuch. Expressly: the names of the shareholders, but not the Aktionäre of the AG. An AG with many shareholders would otherwise force a constantly changing list. The supplier sees other data for the AG, for example firm name, seat, object, and representation, but not every share depot. The exception is the point of the sentence in the theory, not an oversight.

The statement is true.

Contribution amounts apply to GmbH shareholders and limited partners. The entry contains the amount of the capital contributions for limited partners and GmbH shareholders. For the GmbH the supplier therefore sees not only the name but also how high the capital contribution is. That fits liability only with the capital contribution: the quantified contribution is publicly readable. For the AG, by contrast, the names of the Aktionäre are missing; the amount of each private share does not stand there analogously as a member list. Treating the amount for the GmbH as secret erases exactly the point the theory expressly names for GmbH shareholders.

The statement is true.

Power of representation stands in the register. The entry shows who may run the business. For the GmbH that is the managing directors; for the AG the executive board. The supplier should know whose signature binds the company. Exactly that was at the start of the legal-form chapter the question who may conclude contracts. The Firmenbuch answers it for registered enterprises.

The statement is true.

The name duty is swapped. In the Firmenbuch the shareholders of a GmbH stand by name; Aktionäre of an AG by contrast do not. The statement claims the opposite and reverses the rule. A supplier finds the GmbH shareholders there, not the AG Aktionäre. Expecting Aktionäre by name and GmbH shareholders never reads the two forms the wrong way round.

The statement is false.

title: Additional equity in GmbH, AG, and cooperative
context: Three businesses need fresh equity. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: In the GmbH the existing shareholders can increase their contributions or take on an additional shareholder.
In the AG new shares are issued, which either the existing shareholders buy or else new shareholders.
Additional equity of the cooperative is raised by admitting further members.
Through many shareholders who are as a rule liable only with the capital contributed, higher capital sums can more readily be raised.
As soon as an AG issues new shares, all shareholders become personally and unlimitedly liable for all company debts.
tactical_explanations:
Increase contributions or take people in. The overview answers how additional equity is raised for the GmbH thus: the existing shareholders increase their contributions or take on an additional shareholder. Both remain within the GmbH logic of capital contributions, without shares. A growing business therefore need not switch to the AG merely because it wants more equity. The statement captures exactly these two paths.

The statement is true.

New shares, old or new buyers. In the AG new shares are issued, which either the existing shareholders can buy or else new shareholders. Stated capital grows through division into shares, not through a second capital contribution in the GmbH sense. Existing shareholders can go along but need not if others take the new pieces. Exactly so the overview describes the capital increase of the AG.

The statement is true.

More members instead of a statutory minimum capital increase. Through admission of further members comes additional equity. Because entry and exit are simple, membership numbers are easily changeable. It remains: no statutory minimum capital, participation via capital contributions. Assigning the cooperative a duty to issue shares confuses it with the AG.

The statement is true.

Limited liability attracts many capital providers. The idea of the capital company: many shareholders are as a rule liable only with the capital contributed, therefore higher capital sums can more readily be raised. Nobody need put entire private assets as the price of a small stake. GmbH shareholders do that via capital contributions, Aktionäre via buying shares. Exactly for that reason the form suits large capital needs better than a few personally unlimitedly liable persons. Higher capital sums can more readily arise this way because raising capital and management may be separated.

The statement is true.

New shares do not change the type of liability. Aktionäre are not personally liable for the debts of the AG; they risk the money invested in buying shares; the overview says: only with their share capital. Issuing new shares widens the circle or the amounts; it does not turn Aktionäre into OG partners with unlimited liability. The statement hangs on the capital increase a liability rule that the theory of the AG precisely denies.

The statement is false.

title: Neighbourhood bakery as a GmbH
context: A family runs its bakery as a GmbH with an employed managing director. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: As a corporation, the bakery GmbH is a legal person and can conclude contracts in its own name.
The family shareholders are unlimitedly liable with their private assets for all debts of the bakery.
The managing director can run the bakery without being a shareholder.
The share capital of the bakery GmbH must be at least 70,000 euros, because every corporation needs the share capital of an AG.
At least one shareholder is enough for the GmbH.
tactical_explanations:
The bakery itself is the contracting party. Corporations have their own legal personality and can do business and conclude contracts as legal persons. Flour purchases, shop rent and employment contracts run in the name of the GmbH, not necessarily in the private name of each shareholder. Natural persons must act for it, for example the employed managing director; that does not change who holds the rights. One would sue the GmbH, not automatically every family shareholder personally. The statement fits the GmbH as a corporation, not a sole proprietorship behind the same counter where business and person legally coincide.

The statement is true.

Private assets stay outside the capital contribution. GmbH shareholders are liable only with their capital contribution. Unlimited liability with private assets is the rule for the sole proprietorship and OG partners, not the GmbH. If the bakery fails, the family risks what was put into the capital contributions, not automatically house and savings beyond that. The statement hangs the wrong type of liability on the GmbH.

The statement is false.

Employed management is provided for. The managing director can be a shareholder but need not be. The family can hold the capital and appoint a skilled managing director for a salary; the shareholders receive profit shares for their contributions. Capital raising and management may be separated. Anyone who forces identity of family and management ignores exactly this possibility.

The statement is true.

GmbH share capital is at least 10,000 euros; 70,000 euros applies to the AG.

The statement is false.

A one-person GmbH is allowed. There must be at least one shareholder. The family can in theory be condensed to one person or hold several capital contributions; the lower bound is one, not five and not two as with the cooperative. The employed managing director changes nothing about this count of shareholders. The statement hits the founding requirement of the GmbH.

The statement is true.

title: Management board, SCE and supervisory board of the cooperative
context: A growing purchasing cooperative employs more than forty workers. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The cooperative is managed by the management board, which is also formed from cooperative members.
From a certain size of the cooperative — from 40 workers — a supervisory board must be formed.
The European counterpart to the cooperative is the European Cooperative Society or Societas Cooperativa Europaea (SCE).
Profits in the cooperative may neither be reinvested nor paid out to members as rebates.
The number of members is easily changeable because entry and exit are simple.
tactical_explanations:
A management board from its own ranks. Management is by the management board, which is also formed from cooperative members. Management and membership hang together here, unlike the GmbH, whose managing director need not be a shareholder. The highest organ remains the general meeting nonetheless. The statement describes the management level without denying the general meeting.

The statement is true.

Forty employees trigger the supervisory board. From a certain size of the cooperative — from 40 workers — a supervisory board must also be formed. The growing purchasing cooperative crosses this threshold and needs the additional organ beside management board and general meeting. Below that the duty does not apply in this way. Anyone who makes the supervisory board a founding requirement for every two-person cooperative misses the size threshold; anyone who denies it from 40 likewise. The statement hits the book figure and the condition of workers, not a mere member count without employees.

The statement is true.

SCE is the European cooperative, not the SE. The cooperative also has a European counterpart: the European Cooperative Society or Societas Cooperativa Europaea (SCE). The SE is the European public limited company with 120,000 euros minimum capital. Anyone who assigns the SE to the purchasing cooperative reaches for the corporation variant.

The statement is true.

Two permissible paths for profits. Profits are either reinvested in the cooperative or paid out to cooperative members as rebates. "Neither nor" blocks both paths that are named. Joint economic activity is in the foreground; that does not exclude this use of profits. The statement is therefore false.

The statement is false.

Membership is not a rigid share lock. The number of members is easily changeable because it is simple to join a cooperative and also to leave again. So one can also cooperate only temporarily. Additional equity comes through admitting further cooperative members. Exactly this mobility distinguishes the form from a tight, hard-to-expand shareholder circle.

The statement is true.

title: Minimum capital and liability compared
context: Evaluate the following statements comparing GmbH, AG, SE and cooperative:
statements: GmbH shareholders are liable only with their capital contribution, shareholders of an AG only with their share capital.
Cooperative members are liable with their contribution, as a rule in double the amount.
The AG has statutory minimum capital of 70,000 euros, the SE of 120,000 euros, the GmbH of 10,000 euros.
The cooperative has the same statutory minimum capital as the AG.
Managing directors of a GmbH can, but need not, also be shareholders at the same time.
tactical_explanations:
Two corporations, two contribution terms, same direction. The table places side by side: GmbH shareholders only with their capital contribution, AG shareholders only with their share capital. Both are limited liability to the capital invested, not unlimited personal liability. Capital contribution and share capital are the respective labels; they must not be swapped or replaced by private assets. Anyone who assigns the capital contribution to the AG and share capital to the GmbH mixes the forms, but still does not hit the unlimited liability of partnerships.

The statement is true.

Contribution plus the same again, as a rule. Cooperative members are liable with their contribution, as a rule in double the amount. The 100-plus-100 example makes a maximum possible loss of 200 euros from a 100-euro share. That is limited to a certain money amount, not the joint liability of the OG for the total debts. "As a rule" shows that double the amount is the typical case in the book, not an invention outside the text.

The statement is true.

Three statutory thresholds, three forms. GmbH 10,000 euros share capital since 1.1.2024, AG 70,000 euros share capital, SE 120,000 euros. The table bundles AG and SE in one column with exactly these figures. Anyone who inserts 35,000 euros as the applicable GmbH threshold names the value before 1.1.2024, not the current one. The trio in the sentence follows the theory.

The statement is true.

Cooperative and AG do not share the threshold. For the cooperative no minimum capital is necessary; the AG needs 70,000 euros. The same statutory minimum amount would turn the cooperative into a corporation with share capital, which it is not according to the theory. Participation is via capital contributions without a statutory lower bound at the AG level. The statement is false.

The statement is false.

Separation remains possible to the end. The GmbH is led by managing directors; they can be shareholders but need not be. Salary for management, profit shares for the contribution. Capital raising and management may be separated. In the comparison of forms this remains a GmbH feature versus the cooperative, whose management board is formed from cooperative members.

The statement is true.

title: Keeping minimum capital of the legal forms in mind
context: A founder compares legal forms before deciding. Evaluate the following statements on the minimum capital of the legal forms:
statements: A GmbH can already be founded with 10,000 euros minimum share capital.
An AG needs the same minimum capital as a GmbH, because both are corporations.
The Societas Europaea requires with 120,000 euros more minimum capital than the Austrian AG.
A sole proprietorship and an OG manage without a statutory prescribed minimum capital.
A limited partnership needs at least 70,000 euros minimum capital like the AG, because a capital lock is also prescribed by statute for it.
tactical_explanations:
Ten thousand euros open the GmbH. Statutory minimum share capital is 10,000 euros and must be raised overall through the shareholders' capital contributions. It is not a compulsory sum per person, but the lower bound of the company as a whole. Below this amount the statutory capital barrier of the GmbH is missing. The figure is the familiar entry threshold of the corporations.

The statement is true.

Corporation does not mean equal capital. The GmbH requires 10,000 euros, the AG 70,000 euros minimum capital. Both forms limit the liability of shareholders, but set differently high thresholds. Anyone who concludes the same euro amount from the shared category strikes exactly this gap. The AG clearly lies above the GmbH.

The statement is false.

One hundred twenty thousand lie above seventy thousand. The Societas Europaea requires 120,000 euros minimum capital and thus more than the Austrian AG with 70,000 euros. Among the three corporations GmbH, AG and SE, the SE sets the highest threshold. The gap to the AG is 50,000 euros. The European form is the most capital-intensive of the three.

The statement is true.

Without a euro barrier, sole proprietorship and OG start. For both, no statutory minimum capital of this kind is prescribed; in its place stands the unlimited personal liability of the proprietor or partners. Minimum capital is the feature of the corporations GmbH, AG and SE. Anyone who seeks the same capital threshold for partnerships transfers the wrong logic.

The statement is true.

Partnerships such as the KG have no statutory minimum capital; 70,000 euros concerns the AG.

The statement is false.

title: Thinking minimum capital and liability together
context: Evaluate the following statements on the link between minimum capital and liability in the legal forms:
statements: A sole proprietor is personally and unlimitedly liable for the debts of their business, even though no minimum capital is prescribed.
GmbH shareholders are liable only with their capital contribution, not with their private assets, precisely because the GmbH requires statutory minimum capital.
A limited partner is personally and unlimitedly liable for the debts of the KG just like the general partner.
Shareholders of an AG are liable only with their share capital, and the AG requires a higher minimum capital for that than the GmbH.
Because the GmbH requires minimum capital of 10,000 euros, every shareholder is personally liable with their entire private assets for the GmbH debts.
tactical_explanations:
Missing capital barrier and full liability belong together. For the sole proprietorship no minimum capital is prescribed; in return the proprietor is personally and unlimitedly liable with their entire assets. The missing euro threshold is no shield, but the flip side of unlimited liability. Anyone who reads "no minimum capital" as risklessness misunderstands exactly this trade.

The statement is true.

Minimum capital replaces personal liability. In the GmbH shareholders are liable only up to their capital contribution, and in return the company must raise at least 10,000 euros share capital. Limited liability and capital barrier are coupled. Without this threshold the liability limit would be less credible toward creditors. Private assets generally stay outside.

The statement is true.

Two roles, two scopes of liability. In the KG the general partner is personally and unlimitedly liable, the limited partner only up to the amount of their contribution. Anyone who equates both strikes the difference that sets the KG apart from the OG. The limited partner's limited liability is exactly why they do not conduct management. The statement mixes both statuses.

The statement is false.

Higher capital, limited shareholder liability. The AG requires 70,000 euros minimum capital, clearly more than the GmbH's 10,000 euros, and limits shareholders' liability to their share capital. Higher capital barrier and liability limit appear together. The gap to the GmbH explains the higher entry, not personal full liability of the shareholders.

The statement is true.

Minimum capital and limited liability to the capital contribution belong together; private assets are as a rule not liable for GmbH debts.

The statement is false.

title: Who conducts the business?
context: Evaluate the following statements on management in the various legal forms:
statements: In an OG at least two partners jointly conduct the business, because an OG presupposes at least two partners.
In a KG the limited partners may also conduct the business as long as at least one general partner co-decides.
A GmbH needs at least one managing director; that need not be the same person as a shareholder.
Both an AG and an SE are led by a management board.
Because an AG requires 70,000 euros minimum capital, the shareholder who holds the most shares automatically conducts its business.
tactical_explanations:
Two partners run the OG themselves. An OG only comes into being with at least two partners, and these conduct the business. Management and personal liability lie with the same persons; statutory minimum capital is therefore not prescribed for that. The form knows no external management organ such as a management board. Joint management follows from the personal structure.

The statement is true.

Limited partners do not manage. Management of the KG lies with the general partner. The limited partner contributes capital and is liable limitedly up to the contribution, but has no management role. Anyone who makes limited partners managers mixes capital contribution and management authority. Even a co-deciding general partner does not change this basic distribution.

The statement is false.

Managing director and shareholder can come apart. A GmbH needs at least one managing director; that person may be appointed from outside and need not hold a share. Who brings the capital and who conducts the business are separable roles in the GmbH. That distinguishes it from partnerships in which liability and management often coincide.

The statement is true.

A management board leads AG and SE. Both corporations share the same management organ: the management board. They differ in minimum capital (70,000 versus 120,000 euros), not in the organ name. The general meeting appoints the management board; individual shareholders do not manage by virtue of their share package ex officio. The management structure is therefore parallel in both forms.

The statement is true.

Capital amount does not determine the manager. In the AG management lies with the management board, independent of individual shareholders' shareholdings. Appointment is decided by the general meeting, not automatically by the largest single shareholder. The 70,000-euro threshold regulates the capital contribution, not day-to-day management. Anyone who links the two mixes financing and organ rules.

The statement is false.

title: Minimum capital in numerical comparison
context: Three capital companies differ in their minimum capital. Evaluate the following statements on the numerical comparison:
statements: The minimum capital of the AG is seven times as high as that of the GmbH.
The SE lies 50,000 euros above the AG in minimum capital.
Adding the minimum capital amounts of GmbH and AG yields exactly the minimum capital of the SE.
10,000 euros suffice to found a GmbH, but not to found an AG.
Of the three capital companies the SE requires the highest minimum capital.
tactical_explanations:
Seventy divided by ten yields seven. The AG minimum capital of 70,000 euros is therefore seven times the 10,000 euros of the GmbH. This gap explains why many smaller projects choose the GmbH and more capital-intensive ones tend toward AG or SE. The factor seven is pure arithmetic of the two statutory thresholds. It describes the entry difference, not the liability amount per shareholder.

The statement is true.

Fifty thousand euros lie between SE and AG. 120,000 minus 70,000 yields exactly 50,000 euros. The Societas Europaea therefore requires 50,000 euros more than the Austrian AG. The gap is thus fixed by law and independent of comparisons with the GmbH. Within the capital companies the SE remains the dearest formation threshold.

The statement is true.

Ten thousand plus seventy thousand are eighty thousand, not one hundred and twenty. The sum of GmbH and AG minimum capital yields 80,000 euros and does not hit the SE threshold of 120,000 euros. The SE minimum capital is therefore an independently set value, not an addition of the other two amounts. Adding and expecting the SE invents a calculation rule that does not exist.

The statement is false.

Ten suffice for the GmbH, not for the AG. 10,000 euros open GmbH formation but do not suffice for the AG, which requires 70,000 euros. The difference between the two lower limits remains clear. Anyone wanting to found an AG with 10,000 euros undershoots the statutory threshold. The figure only reaches for the smaller capital company.

The statement is true.

SE stands at the top of the trio. Comparing 10,000 euros for the GmbH, 70,000 for the AG, and 120,000 for the SE, the European form requires the highest amount. Within the three capital companies it is therefore the most capital-intensive formation. Neither GmbH nor AG reaches this threshold. Anyone who knows the order recognises the SE at once as the peak value.

The statement is true.

title: Prevalence of legal forms in Austria
context: Evaluate the following statements on the distribution of legal forms in Austria:
statements: The overwhelming majority of Austrian enterprises are Einzelunternehmen, although no statutory minimum capital is prescribed for them.
Because GmbHs with around 10 percent share are clearly rarer than Einzelunternehmen, they also require a lower minimum capital than Einzelunternehmen.
OG and KG each reach a similarly small share in Austria and both need no statutory minimum capital.
Because around 85 percent of Austrian enterprises are Einzelunternehmen, around 85 percent of sales revenue also falls to Einzelunternehmen.
AG and SE occur more rarely in Austria than OG and KG, although their statutory minimum capital lies clearly higher than that of the GmbH.
tactical_explanations:
Frequency and missing capital barrier fit together. Einzelunternehmen make up the largest share of Austrian enterprises and need no statutory minimum capital; in its place stands personal unlimited liability. Many businesses choose this form precisely because of the simple start. Dominance in numbers does not contradict the missing euro threshold.

The statement is true.

Einzelunternehmen have no capital threshold to undercut. The GmbH requires 10,000 euros; for the Einzelunternehmen there is no statutory minimum capital at all. A comparison “lower than Einzelunternehmen” wrongly posits a figure for the latter. Rarity of the GmbH versus Einzelunternehmen also does not explain the height of the GmbH threshold.

The statement is false.

Both small, both without minimum capital. OG and KG each lie at a small single-digit percentage share and both carry no statutory minimum capital. In the OG every partner is fully liable; in the KG the general partner fully and the limited partner limitedly. Similar prevalence and missing euro barrier appear together here; the liability models nonetheless differ.

The statement is true.

Numerical dominance of Einzelunternehmen does not mean the same sales share; GmbHs and large forms contribute disproportionately to sales.

The statement is false.

Rare and expensive: AG and SE. They occur in numbers more rarely than OG and KG, but carry with 70,000 and 120,000 euros a clearly higher minimum capital than the GmbH with 10,000 euros. High capital need is rare; therefore these forms remain numerically behind the partnerships. Rarity and high threshold explain each other.

The statement is true.

title: Who raises the capital?
context: Evaluate the following statements on who raises the capital in the individual legal forms:
statements: In the GmbH the shareholders raise the capital through their capital contributions; in total at least 10,000 euros must be reached.
In the AG the Aktionäre raise the capital by buying shares, and stated capital must amount to at least 70,000 euros.
In the KG only the general partner must make a capital contribution; the limited partner is not obliged to do so.
An AG can raise additional equity by issuing new shares.
A GmbH raises additional equity just like an AG by freely issuing new shares on the stock exchange.
tactical_explanations:
Capital contributions sum to the barrier. GmbH shareholders raise capital through capital contributions that may differ in amount; the sum must reach at least 10,000 euros. Without that sum the statutory capital barrier is missing. Individual contributions may lie below it as long as total capital holds the lower limit. That is the capital mechanics of the GmbH.

The statement is true.

Shares carry the stated capital. In the AG the capital is split into shares that Aktionäre acquire; the lower limit lies at 70,000 euros. Large amounts can thus be spread across many shoulders. Buying the shares is how Aktionäre raise the capital. Below 70,000 euros the statutory stated-capital threshold is missing.

The statement is true.

Duty and possibility are swapped. In the KG the limited partner must make a capital contribution; the general partner may make one but need not, because he is in any case personally unlimitedly liable. The statement reverses duty and possibility. Assigning the contribution duty only to the general partner misreads the limited partner’s role.

The statement is false.

New shares bring fresh equity. The AG can raise additional equity by issuing new shares that existing or new Aktionäre take up. The money flows in as external equity financing. A repayment duty as with a loan does not arise. Capital increase via shares is the typical path of the AG.

The statement is true.

The GmbH knows no freely tradable shares. Additional equity arises there by existing shareholders increasing contributions or by taking on a new shareholder. A stock-exchange issue of new shares as with the AG is not available to the GmbH. Equating both forms on the capital market transfers AG technique to the wrong legal form.

The statement is false.

title: Financing needs at start-up and in operations
context: Evaluate the following statements on why companies raise financial resources:
statements: Adequate financing is already one of the most essential conditions for success at start-up.
For long-term investment in fitted business and office premises, financing must also be available on a long-term basis.
Financing mainly means purchasing machinery; ongoing payments such as wages or rent are not part of financing needs.
Alongside long-term financing needs there is a short-term need, because suppliers often have to be paid earlier than sales revenue comes in.
As soon as the company generates sales, any further financing need disappears, because sales proceeds automatically cover all future payments.
tactical_explanations:
Start-up without money remains theory. Many businesses need premises, equipment and a starting inventory immediately, before the first customer pays. Adequate financing is therefore called one of the most essential conditions for success, not a later cosmetic problem. Anyone who only thinks about funds after the first sale starts with gaps in investments that are made only at longer intervals. Exactly this initial need explains why founders and shareholders contribute funds and why other sources stand alongside them.

The statement is true.

Term and useful life belong together. Business and office premises are long-term investments; the funds for them should likewise be available long-term, otherwise a short-term loan must be repaid while the premises are still used for years. Theory links long-term financing needs expressly to such acquisitions. Short-term supplier credit does not carry a furniture purchase over its useful life. The statement holds this maturity matching without excluding other sources.

The statement is true.

Financing covers investments and ongoing payments — both belong to financing needs.

The statement is false.

Timing gaps create short-term need. Deliveries often have to be paid before sales proceeds come in. Alongside the long-term need for investment funds, a short-term financing need thus arises for the ongoing cycle. Banks and suppliers can close this gap, for example through payment terms. The statement describes exactly this asymmetry between payment to suppliers and later customer payment, not a second start-up.

The statement is true.

Sales fill the till but do not erase the need. After operations begin, sales proceeds again provide funds, yet suppliers often still have to be paid earlier, and investments remain to be financed in addition. The claim that every further need disappears automatically confuses the inflow from sales with full coverage of all future outflows. Long-term acquisitions and recurring ongoing payments remain occasions for financing. The account places both side by side instead of making sales an all-purpose solution.

The statement is false.

title: Equity capital and contributions in kind
context: Evaluate the following statements on equity capital:
statements: Capital that founders or shareholders contribute — including contributions in kind such as delivery vans or PCs — counts as equity capital.
Only cash amounts count as equity capital; contributions in kind do not increase equity capital.
If founders contribute a small delivery van and two PCs alongside money, these contributions in kind also increase equity capital.
Equity capital must as a rule be repaid in full to the providers after a fixed short period.
Equity capital is available to the company long-term, as a rule indefinitely.
tactical_explanations:
Equity capital comprises cash and contributions in kind from the ownership side and need not be repaid.

The statement is true.

Not only the bank account counts. Equity capital includes financial resources and contributions in kind. A vehicle or computer that passes into the business increases the own base just as a bank transfer does. The claim that only cash amounts count strips contributions in kind from the definition. Both are named in one breath and illustrated with the delivery van and two PCs. Without contributions in kind the definition of equity capital would be incomplete.

The statement is false.

Example and rule coincide. If a small delivery van and two PCs are contributed alongside money, these contributions in kind increase equity capital. The account chooses exactly this picture so it is clear: not only the account balance but also usable items count once they belong to the company. The start-up capital base grows by the value of these contributions. Anyone who dismisses them as private toys without capital effect contradicts the example.

The statement is true.

Repayment is precisely not the rule. Equity capital need not be repaid and is therefore available long-term, as a rule indefinitely. A duty to return everything to the providers after a short period would treat equity capital like a time-limited loan. Exactly that is how the table distinguishes: debt capital is time-limited and repayable depending on the agreement; equity capital is not. The statement reverses this feature.

The statement is false.

Indefinite means the normal case for own funds. Because there is no repayment obligation, the contributions as a rule remain with the business without an end date. Equity capital is therefore suitable for long-term investments whose benefits run for years. "As a rule indefinitely" leaves rare contractual special arrangements open but does not change the standard rule. Anyone who thinks of equity capital as a three-month loan misses the time axis of the table.

The statement is true.

title: Equity capital, profits and interest
context: Evaluate the following statements on the consequences of equity capital for interest, distributions and investment:
statements: Equity capital is a possible suitable form of financing for long-term investments.
In periods when no profits are earned, the same interest must be paid on equity capital as on a loan.
When profits are earned, distributions to equity providers may be made, but there is no obligation to do so.
If profits are retained in the company, they increase equity capital.
For many companies it is realistic to finance themselves entirely through equity capital alone and to forgo debt capital.
tactical_explanations:
Term and purpose fit together. Because equity capital need not be repaid and as a rule remains indefinite, it is called a possible suitable form of financing for long-term investments. Machinery, vehicle fleets or computer equipment are acquired only at longer intervals; the funds should last equally long, otherwise repayment pressure arises while the asset is still in use. Suitable does not mean the only possibility: debt capital can also be long-term depending on the agreement, for example as a multi-year bank loan. The statement holds the suitability of own funds without forbidding loans or reinterpreting short-term trade payables as machine financing.

The statement is true.

Interest compulsion hits the loan, not the contribution. On equity capital, in periods without profit, no interest need be paid as on a loan. Creditors usually demand interest regardless of the annual result; equity providers have no such fixed claim in loss years. Equating both burdens in lean years is therefore wrong. Only when profits exist can distributions follow, without that becoming a duty.

The statement is false.

May, but need not. When there are profits, distributions to equity providers may be made, but according to theory there is no obligation to do so. The shareholders can retain rather than withdraw. Exactly this freedom distinguishes profit shares from loan interest, which falls due regardless of management's wish. The statement holds the option and the missing duty.

The statement is true.

Retention strengthens the own base. Profits that remain in the company increase equity capital. That is the same process later called self-financing: internal financing from sales that raises crisis resilience. Distribution reduces this increase; retention enlarges it. The statement describes the capital effect, not the tax return.
