Only after this sequence does the company have a target market on which distinctiveness and the target group's wish make sense.

The statement is true.

Without segments the target market is missing. Positioning is the third phase and presupposes that segments have been formed and selected for cultivation. Before segmentation there would be no such determined target market for the offering. The claim that positioning comes first reverses the scheme. Image and distinctiveness aim at a group already chosen. An image in minds without clarified segments remains undirected, because it is unclear whose perception is to be shaped.

The statement is false.

Perception of important properties. Positioning of the product on the market describes how the product is seen or is to be seen by consumers with regard to important properties. Desired and actual image both belong to it. It is about consumers' view, not only internal feature lists. The statement captures this definition.

The statement is true.

In the second phase it is decided which segments are cultivated — not automatically all equally.

The statement is false.

Selection of segments produces the target market. After the decision which segments are cultivated, the company positions on this target market. The target market is the result of the second phase, not the unfiltered overall market. Phase three builds on this selection. The statement closes the phase sequence correctly. Phase three builds on this segment selection, not on the overall market.

The statement is true.

title: Positioning and unique selling proposition
context: woom GmbH wants to stand out with especially child-suitable, high-quality bicycles that last a long time. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The product should stand out clearly and unmistakably from the competition and be especially desirable for the target group.
The product should attain a unique selling proposition.
For woom GmbH the unique selling proposition is especially child-suitable high-quality bicycles that last a long time.
A unique selling proposition means that the product is identical with competing products in all characteristics.
Positioning and unique selling proposition aim at perception in the chosen target group, not at an arbitrary image in the overall market.
tactical_explanations:
Unmistakable and desirable. The product should stand out clearly and unmistakably from the competition and be especially desirable for the target group. Both together yield the sought position after selection of the target market. Standing out without the target group's wish would remain empty; wish without difference would remain interchangeable. Child suitability without difference from the competition would be interchangeable; difference without the target group's wish would remain a technical add-on.

The statement is true.

USP names the unmistakable advantage. The product should attain a unique selling proposition, that is, exactly that unmistakable position which sets it apart from the competition and makes it especially desirable for the target group. The English expression stands in the theory as the goal of positioning. Without a USP the offering remains interchangeable.

The statement is true.

woom concretises the USP. For woom GmbH the unique selling proposition is especially child-suitable high-quality bicycles that last a long time. Child suitability, quality and durability bundle the difference that parents and children are meant to seek. The statement reproduces the example without excluding other manufacturers; it is this company's formulated USP.

The statement is true.

Identity with the competition would be the opposite. Standing out unmistakably means precisely not being identical in all characteristics. A unique selling proposition requires the difference that the target group sees as an advantage. Complete identity would make positioning superfluous. The statement reverses the definition.

The statement is false.

The target group carries the image. Positioning describes how the product is seen or is to be seen by consumers, and the product should be especially desirable for the target group. After the three phases that is the chosen target market, not an arbitrary image for everyone. woom formulates the USP for child-suitable bikes, not for the entire two-wheeler market without distinction. The statement links phase three with the USP. Anyone who forces the USP onto the overall market without chosen segments again treats every product equally on all markets, although that is usually rejected.

The statement is true.

title: Basic benefit and additional benefit
context: A household buys a bicycle. Evaluate the following statements on the benefit of the product:
statements: Anyone who buys something expects that what is bought will have a benefit.
The basic benefit of a bicycle is riding, that is, the primary purpose of the product.
Additional benefit usually means only the same primary purpose as the basic benefit.
Prestige benefit can consist in being able to afford a particular bike.
Experience benefit can consist in riding being fun or the bike being especially safe.
tactical_explanations:
Purchase is not an end in itself. The technical presentation begins with the point that anyone who buys something expects what is bought to have a benefit. With a notebook that is for example installing and using programmes; location-independent work, low weight or an attractive appearance can come on top. With a bike the core is riding. Product development and later marketing must carefully consider this benefit, otherwise an offering arises that nobody needs. Without expected benefit there would be no reason to pay the price. The statement holds exactly this expectation that product policy puts first.

The statement is true.

Riding is the core, not prestige. As basic benefit the primary purpose of the product is named, and for the bicycle riding is expressly given. Everything else, prestige or experience, stands underneath as additional benefit. Anyone who confuses the basic benefit with a nice paint finish or with the impression that one can afford the bike swaps the two levels. They are deliberately separated: first the purpose, then the benefit beyond that.

The statement is true.

Additional means beyond, not the same purpose again. Additional benefit is the benefit going beyond the basic benefit. Prestige benefit and experience benefit are the two named forms. Reducing additional benefit to the same primary purpose collapses two categories into one. Then prestige would be the same as riding, and the distinction would make no sense. Exactly this equation contradicts the distinction in the presentation.

The statement is false.

Prestige hangs on the bike one can afford. As prestige benefit it is expressly named to be able to afford a particular bike. That is not the basic benefit of riding, but a signal outward: one shows that this model lies within one's means. Product policy must think such additional benefit when planning design and marketing. The statement captures the first of the two additional categories, not a freely invented third.

The statement is true.

Fun and safety lie beyond mere locomotion. Experience benefit is described with two examples: it is fun to ride with it, or it is an especially safe bike. Both presuppose riding but go beyond the primary purpose. Anyone who admits only the basic benefit strikes exactly this second additional form. Product policy should keep customer benefit as a whole in view, basic and additional together.

The statement is true.

title: Four instruments from product policy to communication
context: Evaluate the following statements on product, price, distribution and communication policy:
statements: Product policy belongs to the marketing mix and concerns the offering, which must have a benefit for customers.
Price policy determines among other things how high the price is and which payment terms apply.
Distribution policy deals with how the product reaches the customer, that is, with the sales channel.
Communication policy comprises among other things advertising, sales promotion and public relations.
Of the four areas of the marketing mix only advertising counts; price, place and product design do not belong to it.
tactical_explanations:
Without benefit the offering remains empty. Under the heading product policy it stands first that the product must have a benefit for the customer and that product-policy measures should take customer benefit and the life-cycle phase into account. Product is therefore not decoration but the offering itself; later come price, sales channel and message. Anyone who strikes product policy from the mix drops the first of the four blocks with which the technical presentation works through the mix, and can no longer sensibly align the remaining instruments.

The statement is true.

Level and terms belong together. Price policy is situated between high-price policy and low-price or discount-price policy; in addition payment terms are important. It is therefore not only a number on the price tag, but also how payment is made. The three factors costs, competitor price and willingness to pay steer the setting. The statement stays at this level and invents no own price technique that the theory does not name.

The statement is true.

Path before place. Distribution policy tries to answer two questions: how the product reaches the customer, that is, how the sales channel is to be designed, and which transport route is to be chosen. Place here means the path of the goods, not the company seat. Direct and indirect sales, trade and franchising are expressions of exactly this question. Anyone who confuses distribution with the address of headquarters misses the point.

The statement is true.

Advertising is the entry, not the whole list. Communication policy includes advertising first and foremost, besides that the internet presence, sales promotion, personal selling and public relations including sponsoring and investor relations. Promotion is therefore broader than an advertisement. The statement names three of the expressly listed fields and thus stays within the presentation without anticipating social-media details that follow later.

The statement is true.

Four blocks, not one. The mix section structures product policy, price policy, distribution policy and communication policy one after another. Advertising is only one part of communication, and communication is only one of the four areas. The claim that only advertising counts and that price, place and product design do not belong to it tips the structure. Anyone who reduces the mix to advertisements can explain neither benefit and life cycle nor sales channel and price.

The statement is false.

title: Introduction phase in the life cycle
context: Evaluate the following statements on the introduction phase of a new product:
statements: With the introduction phase the new product is introduced on the market with various advertising measures.
If the product is successful and demanded, sales rise slowly in the introduction phase.
Because development and advertising costs are high, profit is already made on the first day of sale.
Profit is only made towards the end of the introduction phase.
If the product has no success in this phase, it will disappear from the market sooner rather than later.
tactical_explanations:
Introduction means creating visibility. The new product comes onto the market with various advertising measures. Without this introduction potential buyers often would not even know that the offering exists. The technical presentation couples the phase to advertising, not to a silent delivery without communication. Anyone who reads the introduction phase as pure production without a market appearance drops exactly this advertising effort that theory later also names as a cost reason for late profit. Development plus introduction advertising are high, therefore profit does not lie on day one but only towards the end of this phase, if demand arises at all.

The statement is true.

Slowly, not abruptly. With success and demand, sales in this phase rise slowly. That is the typical curve before the strong rise of the growth phase. Anyone who already reads the sales maximum of the maturity phase into this mixes two stages. The slow rise also helps explain why high introduction spending pushes profit back: the curve does not yet carry the upfront costs immediately. If success fails, the strong phase does not come at all.

The statement is true.

Costs stand at the beginning, profit does not. Costs for product development and advertising effort of introduction are high. Therefore profit is only made towards the end of the introduction phase, not on the first day of sale. The absolute early claim ignores exactly this cost burden. A firm that already expects profit on day one has not understood the logic of the phase that is described.

The statement is false.

Towards the end, not at the beginning. Because development and introduction advertising are expensive, profit lies only towards the end of the introduction phase. Before that sales may rise slowly, but they do not yet cover the upfront costs. The statement reproduces the time shift that the foundation expressly sets. Anyone who moves profit into the middle of the growth phase leaves the introduction phase.

The statement is true.

No success, short life. If the product has no success in the introduction phase, it disappears from the market sooner rather than later. It then does not enter the growth phase. The wording "sooner rather than later" comes from the theory and warns against artificially stretching a failed introduction. Product elimination can follow even before maturity or saturation occur at all.

The statement is true.

title: Growth phase and imitators
context: Evaluate the following statements on the growth phase in the product life cycle:
statements: In the growth phase sales rise strongly and with them also profits.
In this phase the competition increasingly becomes aware of the product.
Market potential and market volume denote the same figure: the quantity actually sold.
Price design is decisive in the growth phase in order to expand market position.
In the growth phase sales already reach their maximum while profits are already falling.
tactical_explanations:
Strongly instead of slowly. If the product is successful, it enters the growth phase: sales rise strongly and with them profits. That distinguishes the phase from introduction, in which the rise was still slow and profit arose only late. Anyone who confuses growth with the shrinking market of saturation reads the curve backwards. Here sales and profit grow together before maturity presses profit again even though sales there still reach their maximum. Imitators and price policy already belong in this growth stage, not only in degeneration.

The statement is true.

Visibility attracts competitors. Now the competition increasingly becomes aware of the product. Success is therefore not only one's own curve but a signal to other suppliers. Exactly therefore price design is subsequently named as decisive. Anyone who assumes growth runs without rivals' gaze strikes this sentence of the presentation.

The statement is true.

Market potential is the maximum possible quantity; market volume the quantity actually sold.

The statement is false.

Price as a lever of position. After imitators appear, price design is decisive in order to expand market position. It is not only about covering costs from introduction but about competition for the same benefit. Anyone who treats price as secondary in the growth phase because sales are rising anyway overlooks exactly this fork. Later, in maturity, discounts and promotions come on top as additional expense.

The statement is true.

Maximum and falling profits belong to maturity. The growth phase is followed by the maturity phase, in which sales reach their maximum and profits are already falling again. Anyone who pulls both into the growth phase mixes two stages. In growth, sales and profit still rise together. The confusion is typical because both phases show success; the curve nonetheless separates them sharply.

The statement is false.

title: Maturity phase and saturation phase
context: Evaluate the following statements on maturity and saturation phases:
statements: In the maturity phase sales reach their maximum.
Profits continue to rise in the maturity phase because hardly any advertising effort is still needed.
Profits fall in the maturity phase because increasing competition causes more effort for advertising, discounts and promotions.
In the saturation phase both sales and profits fall, and the market begins to shrink.
Already at the beginning of the saturation phase it must be clear how one wants to proceed with the product.
tactical_explanations:
Sales peak, not profit peak. In the maturity phase sales reach their maximum. That is the indicator of this stage, not automatically profit. Anyone who equates maximum with further rising profits overlooks the next point. The peak of sales coincides with rising advertising and promotion effort that already presses profit.

The statement is true.

Advertising becomes more expensive, not superfluous. Because of increasing competition, ever more effort for advertising and other sales-promoting measures arises — discounts and promotions. Therefore profits already fall in maturity even though sales are at their maximum. The claim that hardly any advertising is still needed and profits continue to rise reverses the cost logic. Maturity is no sheltered space but an expensive defence fight for the same market. Anyone who attributes falling profits only to saturation overlooks that the decline already starts here, before the market begins to shrink.

The statement is false.

Competition drives the effort. Ever more advertising, discounts and promotions are the reason that profits already fall again in maturity. Sales promotion here is a means against rivals, not mere decoration. The statement reproduces mechanism and direction correctly. Anyone who places the profit decline only in degeneration overlooks that it already starts in maturity, before the market shrinks.

The statement is true.

Both figures fall, the market shrinks. In the saturation phase sales and profits fall; the market begins to shrink. That is sharper than maturity, in which sales were still at their maximum. Shrinking means: even the cake becomes smaller, not only one's own slice. Exactly therefore the further strategy must already be fixed at the beginning of this phase, before high costs of degeneration threaten.

The statement is true.

Decide early, not in degeneration. Already at the beginning of the saturation phase it must be clear how one wants to proceed with the product, before it enters the degeneration phase. Waiting until the pure cost phase is too late. Elimination or relaunch are named in the next paragraph exactly as this prior decision.

The statement is true.

title: Degeneration, elimination and relaunch
context: Evaluate the following statements on the end of the product life cycle:
statements: In the degeneration phase the product causes only high costs.
Whether one removes the product from the offering or tries a relaunch with a product change must already be clear before the degeneration phase.
Product elimination means taking a product that is no longer successful off the market.
A relaunch tries a restart with a product change.
A company may only think about elimination or relaunch in the degeneration phase, because no costs arise beforehand.
tactical_explanations:
Only costs left, hardly any return. In the degeneration phase the product causes only high costs. Sales and profit have already fallen in saturation; now the burden remains. Therefore the decision on further handling should not fall only here. Anyone who reads degeneration as a quiet residual phase without cost pressure contradicts the wording. The phase is the endpoint one wants to avoid or steer, not the moment of first reflection.

The statement is true.

Clarify beforehand, not afterwards. It must already be clear beforehand whether one removes the product from the offering or tries a restart with a product change — a relaunch. "Beforehand" refers to the time before degeneration, linking to the beginning of saturation in which sales and profit are already falling and the market begins to shrink. Anyone who makes the choice only when only costs are running acts against the time requirement. Elimination and relaunch are the two named paths, not a third unnamed middle way as a duty. Product-policy measures should steer the cycle, not only comment after collapse.

The statement is true.

Take off the market when success is missing. Product elimination is the measure by which a product that is no longer successful is taken off the market. It stands beside innovation and variation in the list of product-policy measures. The aim is not to stretch the life cycle artificially in the cost zone. The statement repeats the definition and invents no additional condition such as a legal duty to strike.

The statement is true.

Change as a second start. Instead of removing, one can try a restart with a product change; relaunch is set beside it in parentheses. That is not the same variation in which only the new version runs, but it is related: one changes in order to stretch the cycle. Product-policy measures overall serve to shape the life cycle as optimally as possible and to prolong success. Relaunch is exactly this attempt at the late edge.

The statement is true.

Costs arise far earlier. Development and advertising costs already burden introduction; in maturity advertising and promotion costs rise; in saturation sales and profit fall. Degeneration is the endpoint with only high costs left, not the first cost point. The claim that one may only then think about elimination or relaunch because no costs arose beforehand is false in both halves. Theory requires clarification already beforehand.

The statement is false.

title: Product differentiation and product diversification
context: woom GmbH expands its offering. Evaluate the following statements on product-policy innovations:
statements: If woom GmbH offers further bike models in addition to existing bikes, it deepens its bike assortment and practises product differentiation.
If besides bikes it also offers sports equipment and fitness devices, it widens the assortment; that would be product diversification.
Further bike models beside the existing bikes are product diversification, because each model opens an entirely new field of business.
Product innovation can complement existing products and make the assortment deeper or wider.
Product differentiation and product diversification are the same word in the theory, because both only deepen the assortment.
tactical_explanations:
Depth in the same assortment. Further models of bikes in addition to the existing bikes deepen the bike assortment; that is called product differentiation. The field remains bicycle; only the variants become more. woom serves here as an example, not as a compulsory exam brand. Anyone who already calls this deepening diversification confuses depth with width. Diversification would be only the admission of quite different goods groups beside the bikes, for example sports equipment and fitness devices. Innovation is the umbrella term; the direction decides the name.

The statement is true.

Width into new goods groups. Sports equipment, clothing, rain protection and fitness devices beside bikes would widen the assortment; that would be product diversification. New product fields step beside the core business. The direction is width, not yet another bike model. The statement follows the second woom example faithfully and keeps the distinction from differentiation.

The statement is true.

Models deepen; they do not open a new field. Additional bike models are differentiation, not diversification. Diversification would be widening for example through sports equipment. The claim that each model is a new field of business and therefore diversification tips the pairing deeper versus wider. A further children's bike remains in the bike assortment even if it looks different.

The statement is false.

Innovation complements and shapes the assortment. Various forms of product innovation complement existing products and make the assortment deeper — product differentiation — or wider — product diversification. Innovation is here the umbrella term; the two forms describe the direction. Anyone who thinks of innovation only as complete replacement of the old programme drops the complementarity logic. Variation changes an existing product and takes the old version off the market; elimination takes an unsuccessful product entirely. Both stand beside innovation but do not replace it as assortment deepening or widening.

The statement is true.

Deeper and wider are two directions. Differentiation deepens, diversification widens. They are not the same word and they do not both deepen. The equation strikes exactly the distinction that the woom example is meant to carry. Without it one could no longer say whether new models or entirely new goods groups are meant.

The statement is false.

title: Product variation and market entry
context: Evaluate the following statements on product variation and on entry into the market:
statements: In product variation an existing product is changed.
In product variation only the changed new version is still offered, the preceding version no longer.
Product variation means permanently carrying old and new version in parallel in the assortment.
Going into the market first can mean higher entrepreneurial risks, for example market-opening costs for development and communication.
A company can also wait to see how the market develops and then follow with a similar product.
tactical_explanations:
Change to the existing good. Product variation means an existing product is changed. It is not about an additional model beside the old one in the sense of differentiation, but about changing what was already there. The measure stands in the list beside innovation and elimination. Anyone who confuses variation with merely adding a further unchanged article misses this point. Decisive is the following sentence: only the new version remains; the preceding one is no longer offered. Exactly that separates variation from a deeper assortment complement in which old models may continue to run.

The statement is true.

Only the new version remains. Expressly: only the changed new version is still offered, the preceding version no longer. The old offering disappears with the variation. Exactly that distinguishes it from differentiation, in which further models complement the existing ones. The statement is the rule, not an interpretation.

The statement is true.

Parallel operation is not the usual variation. Because the preceding version is no longer offered, old and new may not permanently stand side by side. Anyone who claims parallelism describes rather an assortment deepening than variation. The confusion is close because both look "new"; the criterion is whether the old version disappears.

The statement is false.

Being first costs. Already at entry one must consider whether one can dare to go into the market first with higher entrepreneurial risk. In parentheses market-opening costs are named, for example arising development and communication costs. Pioneer role is therefore not mere prestige but a cost and risk question.

The statement is true.

Following remains the second option. One can rather wait to see how the market develops and then follow with a similar product. That is the counter-strategy to early entry with market-opening costs. Both paths serve to shape the life cycle as optimally as possible. Anyone who thinks only the pioneer is admissible strikes the named alternative.

The statement is true.

title: Price setting and demand
context: Evaluate the following statements on price policy:
statements: If many products with roughly the same benefit compete, price policy plays a decisive role.
Price policy is situated between high-price policy and low-price policy or discount-price policy.
For setting the price, the costs of the product, the price of comparable competing products and customers' willingness to pay are significant.
Charging a higher price than customers can or want to pay is fundamentally sensible, because higher prices secure sales.
In addition to the price level, payment terms are important.
tactical_explanations:
Same benefit sharpens the price. If many products and services whose benefit for takers is roughly the same compete, price policy plays a decisive role. Favourable prices are then relevant for example with food, everyday clothing, flights or mobile tariffs. If by contrast the USP is established, many also pay higher prices. The statement captures the first case in which price tips the scales.

The statement is true.

Two poles, practice in between. Price policy is situated between high-price policy and low-price policy or discount-price policy. Theory spans exactly this range without defining intermediate forms as a compulsory own strategy. Payment terms come on top. Anyone who thinks only one of the poles is the only allowed policy narrows the span. The statement reproduces the situation correctly.

The statement is true.

Three factors, not one. In practice there are mainly three factors: How high are the costs; can they at least be covered with the price? How high is the price for a comparable competing product? How much are customers willing to pay? Costs, rivals and willingness to pay together steer the setting. Anyone who admits only cost-plus logic and strikes the other two undercuts the list.

The statement is true.

Lying above willingness to pay is of little sense. Charging a higher price than customers can or want to pay is of little sense. Fundamentally, at high prices demand is normally low and at low prices high. The claim that a too-high price is sensible because high prices always increase demand twists both sentences. The three factors costs, competitor price and willingness to pay set an upper limit on the level. Snob, bandwagon and quality effects are later exceptions in which expensive is bought; they do not make overpricing beyond ability and willingness a general success rule.

The statement is false.

Terms beside the amount. In addition, payment terms are important. Price policy is therefore not only the level but also how and under which conditions payment is made. That stands directly after the span between high and low price. Anyone who excludes terms from price policy drops an expressly named building block.

The statement is true.

title: Seller's market and buyer's market
context: Evaluate the following statements on seller's market and buyer's market:
statements: If demand exceeds supply, one speaks of a seller's market.
On a seller's market sellers find it easier than the buyer side to influence the price.
In the long run a seller's market often leads to several companies producing the desired good, supply rising and prices falling again.
If supply exceeds demand, a buyer's market arises in which buyers have more bargaining power.
On a buyer's market prices rise permanently, because the buyer side has no bargaining power at all.
tactical_explanations:
Demand above supply. If demand exceeds supply, one speaks of a seller's market. The definition hangs on the quantity relation, not on the industry name. Here prices are rather high or tend to rise. Anyone who uses the same name for the case in which supply exceeds demand swaps seller's and buyer's market.

The statement is true.

Power lies with those who offer scarce goods. On the seller's market sellers find it easier than buyers to influence the price. As a buyer one has comparatively little bargaining power and design room. The price advantage of the supplier side follows from scarcity relative to demand. The statement reproduces exactly this asymmetry.

The statement is true.

Supply catches up, prices fall. In the long run a seller's market often leads to several companies producing the desired good, supply thereby rising and prices falling again. High prices and easy sales attract additional production. The market therefore does not permanently stay on the seller side. If supply subsequently exceeds demand, the buyer's market arises with more power on the demand side. Anyone who thinks of the situation as eternal high price without reaction by suppliers ignores exactly this long-term movement that theory attaches to the seller's market.

The statement is true.

Supply above demand tips the power. If supply then exceeds demand, a buyer's market arises. There buyers can influence prices and have more bargaining power. The definition is the mirror image of the seller's market. In the long run prices fall until some suppliers no longer sell at that price and supply declines.

The statement is true.

Power and price direction are swapped. In the buyer's market the buyer side has more bargaining power, not no power at all. Prices fall in the long run until suppliers exit; thereafter supply can decline and prices rise again. Permanently rising prices with powerless buyers rather describe a seller's market. The statement mixes both market forms and is false.

The statement is false.

title: Snob, bandwagon and quality effects
context: Evaluate the following statements on price changes and on reactions that are not fully rational:
statements: Fundamentally, at high prices demand is normally low and at low prices high.
Customers' reactions to price changes are regularly fully rational.
With the snob effect one buys expensive in order to show that one can afford it.
With the bandwagon effect one buys expensive because others do so too.
With the quality effect one suspects that expensive products are better than cheaper ones and therefore buys the more expensive.
tactical_explanations:
Normal price–quantity direction. Fundamentally, at high prices demand is normally low and at low prices high. As a rule high demand means prices can be raised somewhat; if demand falls, prices are often lowered. That is the starting rule before the exceptions. Anyone who denies it can no longer recognise snob and quality effects as deviation.

The statement is true.

Not always rational. Customers' reactions to price changes are not always fully rational. Snob effect, bandwagon effect and quality effect are to be taken into account. The word "regularly" / "always" in the statement turns the rule into an absolute that theory expressly relativises. The three effects are exactly the named deviations in which expensive is bought even though the normal curve at high prices would rather expect low demand. Snob shows affordability, bandwagon follows others, quality suspects better in the expensive good. None of these three motives cancels the basic rule; they only limit the claim of full rationality.

The statement is false.

Showing that one can afford it. With the snob effect one buys expensive in order to show that one can afford it. The motive is prestige, not the cheapest benefit per euro. A high price can even support demand of this group, against the normal rule. The statement captures the definition and does not mix it with following other buyers.

The statement is true.

Others do it too. With the bandwagon effect one buys expensive because others do so too. Joining the group, not the individual prestige signal of the snob, is the motive. Both effects can carry the same high price but for different reasons. Anyone who equates bandwagon with the suspicion of better quality reaches for the third effect that theory lists separately.

The statement is true.

Expensive counts as better. With the quality effect one suspects that expensive products are better than cheaper ones, so one buys the more expensive. The price figure becomes a quality indicator, independently of whether costs justify it. That stands beside snob and bandwagon as a third not fully rational reaction to price. The statement reproduces the suspicion and the purchase consequence correctly.

The statement is true.

title: Direct and indirect sales
context: Evaluate the following statements on distribution policy:
statements: Distribution policy tries to clarify how the sales channel is to be designed and which transport route is chosen.
In direct sales the producing company sells directly to the end customer.
In indirect sales one or more trading firms are interposed on the path between producer and end customer.
In direct sales wholesale and retail are regularly interposed between producer and end customer.
If one orders directly from the producer, who fulfils from headquarters or an own branch, it is a direct sales channel.
tactical_explanations:
Two questions, one policy field. Distribution policy tries to answer two essential questions: how the product reaches the customer, that is, how the sales channel is to be designed, and which transport route is to be chosen. Place is thus organisation of the path, not only a sign at the warehouse. Anyone who thinks only of the lorry without the question of intermediaries drops the sales channel. Direct to the end customer or indirect via wholesale and retail, plus franchising: those are answers to the first question. Both questions stand at the beginning and carry the rest of distribution policy.

The statement is true.

Without trade in between. In direct sales the producing company sells directly to the end customer. No wholesaler or retailer stands in between. The later order from the producer from headquarters or branch is exactly this case. Anyone who already values every branch as indirect sales even though it belongs to the producer blurs the boundary that theory draws.

The statement is true.

Trade in between. In indirect sales one or more trading firms are interposed on the sales path between producer and end customer. That includes wholesalers who sell on to other traders, and retailers who sell to the final consumer. One link suffices; several are possible. The statement holds the definition without anticipating franchising.

The statement is true.

Direct sales means sale without interposed trading firms. Wholesale and retail characterise the indirect path.

The statement is false.

Headquarters or branch remain direct. If one orders directly from the producer, who fulfils the order from its headquarters or also from an own branch, it is a direct sales channel. The own branch is not an independent trading firm in between. Anyone who equates it with a foreign retailer turns direct sales into indirect. Both fulfilment places are expressly named as direct.

The statement is true.

title: Franchising as a sales channel
context: Evaluate the following statements on franchising:
statements: In franchising the franchisor makes brand name, products and marketing know-how available to the franchisee against payment of a franchise fee.
The franchise fee usually consists of a fixed amount plus a share of sales.
The franchisee is economically and legally independent.
The franchisee is bound to the assumed marketing concept and business model of the franchisor to the agreed extent.
The franchisee loses all legal independence and becomes an unindependent branch of the franchisor.
tactical_explanations:
Name, goods and know-how against a fee. Franchising is a special sales channel: the franchisor makes its brand name, its products and its entire marketing know-how available to another company, the franchisee, against payment of a franchise fee — for example shop design, advertising and internet presence. It is not a mere supply contract without a concept. The fee is usually a fixed amount plus a share of sales; the franchisee remains economically and legally independent, bound only to the agreed extent. The statement bundles performance and consideration as listed, without already striking independence.

The statement is true.

Fixed plus sales. The fee is usually a fixed amount plus a share of sales. Both together, not only a one-off lump sum without an ongoing share, describe the usual pattern. Concrete euro amounts are not named; the structure suffices. Anyone who strikes the sales share undercuts "usually fixed amount plus sales share".

The statement is true.

Independent despite the concept. The franchisee is economically and legally independent. It remains another company, not an unindependent operating part. Exactly that makes franchising a special sales channel between the parties, not a mere branch foundation. The next binding to the concept does not turn independence into its opposite.

The statement is true.

Binding to the agreed extent. Despite independence the franchisee is bound to the assumed marketing concept and business model of the franchisor to the agreed extent. Uniform appearance is the point of transferring know-how. The binding is contractually limited, not boundless and not zero. Anyone who reads every prescription as loss of legal personality goes beyond the business logic; anyone who denies every binding turns franchise into free resale without a concept.

The statement is true.

A branch would not be independence. Legally independent and at the same time bound to the concept: that is the combination. An unindependent branch would strike legal independence. The statement asserts exactly this loss and is false. Franchise remains a contract between two companies, not the conversion of the franchisee into an establishment without its own legal personality.

The statement is false.

title: Advertising media and advertising carriers
context: Evaluate the following statements on classic advertising in communication policy:
statements: Communication policy includes advertising first and foremost.
Advertisements or inserts are advertising media; daily and weekly magazines can be advertising carriers.
TV spots and radio spots use television and radio as advertising carriers.
Advertising media and advertising carriers denote the same object with two arbitrary names.
Posters and advertising boards can be disseminated via billboards, advertising columns or public transport facilities.
tactical_explanations:
Advertising first, not alone. Communication policy includes advertising first and foremost, as known classically in the forms of the overview: advertisements in magazines, spots on radio and television, posters on walls and columns, letters and brochures via distributors. "First and foremost" means priority in the technical logic, not that sales promotion, personal selling and PR are missing. The statement captures this entry. Anyone who derives from it that communication is only advertising would go further than the wording; here only the priority is asserted that stands in the theory before website, actions and publicity follow.

The statement is true.

Medium versus carrier. Advertising media and advertising carriers are set side by side. Advertisements (inserts) stand as media; daily and weekly magazines, illustrated magazines, trade journals and event programmes as carriers. The medium is the designed message; the carrier is the channel that transports it. Anyone who collapses advertisement and magazine into one makes the distinction superfluous.

The statement is true.

Spot is medium, broadcaster is carrier. TV and radio spots use television and radio as advertising carriers. The same two-part division applies with advertisement and magazine. A spot without a broadcaster would be medium without carrier. The statement assigns both sides of the communication chain correctly. The same two-part division applies analogously with advertisement and magazine.

The statement is true.

Two columns, two roles. The overview separates advertising media and advertising carriers. They would be arbitrary synonyms only if advertisement and magazine were the same. They are not: the one is designed, the other carries it. The statement asserts identity and is false. Anyone who gives up the separation can also no longer distinguish poster and billboard.

The statement is false.

Surface as carrier of the poster. Posters and advertising boards are media; billboards, advertising columns, public transport facilities and sports grounds are named as carriers. The statement names three of the carriers correctly. It stays within classic advertising and does not yet reach for blogs or social media, which later get their own sentences.

The statement is true.

title: Sales promotion, personal selling and public relations
context: Evaluate the following statements on further instruments of communication policy:
statements: Communication policy includes the company's entire presence on the internet with its own website and in social networks.
Sales promotion through particular actions belongs to communication policy.
The behaviour of sales staff, called personal selling in the theory, counts as communication policy.
Public relations often relates to the whole company, for example press conferences, press releases, targeted information of investors and sponsoring.
Communication policy as a rule concerns only the individual product and usually not the company as a whole.
tactical_explanations:
Online presence is communication. Besides various forms of advertising, the company's entire presence on the internet with its own website and in social networks belongs to communication policy. It is not only a technical appendage of distribution, even if the sales channel can run in parallel online. Anyone who takes website and networks out of promotion strikes the first of the four points after classic advertising. Social-media marketing later deepens the same idea as advertising and PR on platforms such as Facebook and X. Here first the assignment of the presence to communication counts.

The statement is true.

Actions promote sales. Sales promotion through particular actions stands expressly on the list. In the maturity phase discounts and promotions were already named as costly measures against competition; here they belong to communication policy. The statement stays with "particular actions" and invents no duty to book every price cut as promotion. It holds the assignment to the mix instrument Promotion.

The statement is true.

People at the point of sale. The behaviour of sales staff is assigned to communication policy as personal selling. The message runs not only via advertisement and spot but via conversation. Anyone who thinks of personal selling only as personnel management without customer reference takes the English expression out of the marketing mix. As a measure it stands in parentheses exactly behind behaviour at the sale.

The statement is true.

PR often aims at the organisation. Communication policy also often relates not only to the products but to the whole company, for example in the area of public relations. PR comprises press conferences, press releases, targeted information of particular target groups — for example investors as investor relations — as well as sponsoring. The statement summarises this palette. It does not turn PR into a product advertisement under another name.

The statement is true.

Product and company. Precisely PR shows that communication often concerns the whole company, not exclusively the individual product. The absolute restriction "only" and "usually not" contradicts this point. Advertising can put the product in the foreground; PR, investor relations and sponsoring widen the view. The statement is therefore too narrow and false.

The statement is false.

title: Social-media marketing and event marketing
context: Evaluate the following statements on social-media marketing and event marketing:
statements: Social-media marketing as a rule denotes advertising and PR of a company in social media such as Facebook and X.
Public relations by means of social media is called social media relations.
Via social media companies can quickly and directly contact many potential customers, present products and communicate messages.
Event marketing comprises experience-oriented events that are meant to trigger a strong activation process in the customer.
Event marketing as a rule is limited only to internal staff training without outward effect on customers.
tactical_explanations:
SMM as advertising and PR in networks. Social-media marketing denotes marketing activities — as a rule advertising and PR — of a company in social media such as Facebook and X, formerly Twitter. It is therefore not a fifth P beside the four instruments, but communication on these platforms. User numbers have risen many times over; importance has increased enormously. Public relations there is called social media relations. The statement stays with the rule "advertising and PR" and invents no own compulsory indicators. Contact, product presentation and mood follow in the next paragraph as effect, not as own definition.

The statement is true.

Relations as the name of public relations. Public relations by means of social media is called social media relations. That parallels PR with a channel-related expression. Anyone who equates relations with pure banner placement without public relations narrows the name expressly introduced. The statement reproduces the designation that is expressly introduced.

The statement is true.

Direct, quick, many addressees. Via social media companies can quickly and directly contact a multitude of potential customers, present products, communicate messages and create positive mood for themselves and their products. That is the reason why SMM has gained importance. Anyone who thinks of social media only as a one-sided billboard without contact possibility drops "directly contact".

The statement is true.

Experience and activation. Event marketing comprises experience-oriented events that are meant to trigger a strong activation process in the customer. They are meant to direct attention to a company, a product group or an event: fashion shows, trade fairs, exhibition and shop openings, cultural and sports events. The statement captures the definition before the example series. Activation is the goal, not silent information without experience.

The statement is true.

Outward to the customer, not only internal. The named events direct attention to company, product group or event and are meant to activate customers. Internal staff training without outward effect does not stand in this list. The restriction "exclusively internal" strikes fashion show, trade fair and sports event. Event marketing is a communication instrument outward, complementary to advertising and SMM.

The statement is false.

title: Absolute and relative market share (15/100/30)
context: An Austrian bicycle manufacturer A achieves revenue of 15 million euros in a value market of 100 million euros; the largest competitor turns over 30 million euros. Evaluate the following statements on absolute and relative market share:
statements: The absolute market share of company A is 15 percent, because its revenue makes up 15 percent of the market volume of 100 million euros.
The relative market share of company A is 0.5, because its revenue is half as high as that of the largest competitor.
Because the relative market share of A is smaller than one, A can nonetheless still be the market leader.
Relative market share arises by dividing A's revenue by the entire market volume.
If A's revenue were as high as that of the largest competitor, relative market share would lie at exactly one.
tactical_explanations:
Fifteen of one hundred are 15 percent. Absolute market share relates own revenue to market volume: 15 million euros of 100 million euros. The revenue of the largest competitor does not belong in this denominator; it only steers relative market share. The statement captures the absolute indicator. Rival revenue belongs only in the relative market-share formula.

The statement is true.

Half as much as the rival yields 0.5. Relative market share relates 15 million euros to the revenue of the strongest competitor of 30 million euros. The indicator describes a ranking, not a share of the overall market. Below one means: smaller than the previously strongest. The statement calculates correctly. Below one means: smaller than the previously strongest competitor.

The statement is true.

A relative market share below one means that own revenue is accordingly smaller than that of the strongest rival — that precisely rules out market leadership in this indicator. Market leader would only be a company with a relative market share above one, that is, with revenue above that of the previously largest competitor.

The statement is false.

The entire market volume belongs in the absolute, not the relative formula. Relatively, own revenue is divided by the revenue of the largest competitor. Anyone who instead puts market volume in the denominator confuses both indicators and loses the comparison with the strongest rival.

The statement is false.

A tie yields relatively one. If own revenue is as high as that of the largest competitor, the quotient is accordingly exactly one. Only above that does market leadership in the sense of this indicator begin. Below one one remains behind the rival. The threshold of one marks the tie. Only a quotient above one signals market leadership.

The statement is true.

title: Distinguishing market potential and market volume
context: A manufacturer of everyday bikes knows its market potential at 80,000 units, actual market volume at 48,000 units and own sales at 6,000 units. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: The market potential of 80,000 units describes the maximum possible sales quantity, not the quantity already actually sold.
The market volume of 48,000 units is already the maximum possible sales that the market allows at all.
Because market volume lies clearly below market potential, this market is almost saturated.
The sales volume of company A of 6,000 units corresponds to the entire market volume.
Between market potential and market volume, 32,000 units of unused room for additional sales remain.
tactical_explanations:
Eighty thousand are the imagined upper limit. Market potential describes how large the market would be if all with a fulfilable need bought; it is accordingly not an actual figure. At 80,000 units it lies above market volume of 48,000. Anyone who reads potential as already sold confuses maximum and actual. That follows directly from the named figures.

The statement is true.

Forty-eight thousand are actual, not maximum. Market volume is accordingly the quantity actually sold; the upper limit is called market potential and lies at 80,000 units. Anyone who swaps both confuses actual and maximum figure. The statement wrongly turns volume into the absolute ceiling. The upper limit is called market potential and here lies at 80,000 units.

The statement is false.

Sixty percent of the upper limit is not almost saturated. 48,000 of 80,000 leave a gap of 32,000 units. Almost saturated would the market only be if volume moved close to potential. Here ample unused room remains. The statement massively overestimates saturation. With a gap of 32,000 units the market remains clearly unsaturated.

The statement is false.

Six thousand are a part, not the whole. A's sales volume is accordingly only a slice of market volume of 48,000 units; other suppliers contribute the rest. A single company cannot be the entire market volume as long as competitors sell effectively. The statement equates part and sum. Other suppliers contribute the rest of market volume.

The statement is false.

The difference marks the room. 80,000 minus 48,000 yields 32,000 units between potential and volume. As long as this gap exists, theoretically more could still be sold. The number is accordingly pure subtraction of the two market figures. The statement captures exactly this unused remainder. The 32,000 units are pure subtraction of potential and volume.

The statement is true.

title: An almost saturated market in figures
context: A regional market for city bikes has a market potential of 50 million euros and a market volume of 48 million euros; company A turns over 8 million euros, the largest competitor 12 million euros. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: Because the market volume of 48 million euros lies close to the market potential of 50 million euros, this market counts as almost saturated.
In an almost saturated market, sales to the same unchanged need-holders can hardly still be increased.
The absolute market share of company A is 16 percent, because one divides its revenue by market potential instead of by market volume.
The relative market share of company A is two thirds, because its revenue makes up two thirds of the revenue of the largest competitor.
An almost saturated market can in no way be turned back into an unsaturated market.
tactical_explanations:
Forty-eight of fifty million are 96 percent. Market volume lies close under market potential; if the actual moves so close to the theoretical upper limit, the market counts as almost saturated. Additional sales to the same need-holders become tight. The figures show saturation, not a wide gap. The statement captures this relation.

The statement is true.

Almost all reachable need-holders already buy. The residual gap of 50 minus 48 equals 2 million euros leaves hardly any room for additional sales to the unchanged buyer circle. Growth then requires new products or new target groups. To the same unchanged need-holders, increase is accordingly hardly possible. The statement describes exactly this tightness.

The statement is true.

Absolute market share needs market volume as denominator. Own revenue of 8 million euros is accordingly to be related to 48 million euros, not to the potential of 50 million euros. Anyone who divides by potential chooses the wrong, too large reference figure and obtains 16 percent instead of about 16.7 percent on a volume basis. The statement expressly names the wrong denominator.

The statement is false.

Eight to twelve are two thirds. Relative market share compares own revenue with that of the largest competitor: 8 divided by 12 yields about 0.67. Below one means no market leadership, but the calculation is accordingly correct. The indicator measures rank, not share of the overall market. The statement captures the quotient. The indicator measures ranking, not share of the overall market.

The statement is true.

Saturation is accordingly not an end state. Through changed products or new buyer groups the circle of need-holders can be widened so that room between volume and potential arises again. An almost saturated market can thus be opened again. The claim of an unchangeable state contradicts these opening strategies.

The statement is false.

title: Calculating revenue shares of several suppliers
context: A value bicycle market of 100 million euros is distributed among company A with 40 million euros, the largest competitor B with 25 million euros and supplier C with 20 million euros (remainder: other suppliers). Evaluate the following statements on the revenue shares:
statements: If A turns over 40 million euros in a 100-million-euro market, its absolute market share is 40 percent.
A's largest competitor is automatically the one with the highest revenue among all remaining suppliers.
If A's revenue is higher than that of the largest competitor, A's relative market share lies above one and A counts as market leader.
A's relative market share results from dividing its revenue by the entire market volume.
A supplier with lower revenue than A can nonetheless have a higher relative market share than A if it lies closer to the revenue of the largest competitor.
tactical_explanations:
Forty of one hundred are 40 percent. Absolute market share relates own revenue to market volume. The revenues of the other suppliers do not change this own share; they only explain the remaining 60 percent. B and C do not belong in the denominator of this indicator. The statement calculates the own share correctly.

The statement is true.

Largest competitor means highest revenue among the others. Not A itself, but the strongest of the other suppliers forms the denominator of the relative market-share formula. This definition steers with whom comparison is made. If the strongest rival changes, the denominator changes. The statement captures exactly this selection rule. If the strongest rival changes, this denominator also changes.

The statement is true.

Above one means market leader in the relative sense. If own revenue exceeds that of the previously strongest rival, the quotient is greater than one. Exactly that marks market leadership in this indicator. Below one one remains behind the rival. The statement links quotient and leadership correctly. Below one one remains behind the strongest competitor.

The statement is true.

Market volume belongs in the absolute market-share formula. Relatively, own revenue is divided by the revenue of the largest competitor, not by the entire market volume. The confusion erases the direct comparison with the strongest rival and makes the threshold of one meaningless.

The statement is false.

This point: relative market share measures the ratio of two revenues to the revenue of the largest competitor, not the proximity of two numbers to each other. A supplier with lower own revenue cannot achieve a higher quotient than a supplier with higher revenue if both use the same rival as reference; the quotient grows with the numerator, not with optical proximity of the numbers.

The statement is false.

title: Sales potential and sales volume of an individual company
context: A producer of children's bikes (company A) knows market potential at 20,000 units, market volume at 12,000 units, its own sales potential at 4,000 units, its sales volume at 2,400 units and the sales of the largest competitor at 3,000 units. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: A company's sales potential is the quantity it can reach in the best case or hopes to reach, not the sales already realised.
Sales potential and sales volume of a company are different indicators; potential can lie above actual volume.
The sales potential of an individual company is conceptually the same as the market potential of the entire market.
A company's absolute market share in quantity terms results from its sales volume in relation to market volume, not in relation to its own sales potential.
A company whose sales volume lies below the sales volume of the largest competitor can nonetheless reach a relative market share above one.
tactical_explanations:
Sales potential is best case, not actual. It describes the quantity the company can reach in the best case or hopes to reach. Typically it lies above actual sales, because unused chances still remain. Anyone who equates potential and volume strikes the growth room. The statement separates both clearly.

The statement is true.

Two indicators, often apart. Sales potential is the sought best case, sales volume the realised sales. As long as chances are open, potential lies above actual volume. Both figures belong to the company but measure target and actual separately. The statement holds exactly this difference. Target figure and actual sales deliberately measure different things.

The statement is true.

Market potential relates to the entire market and all need-holders; sales potential only to an individual company and its own best-case quantity. An individual company cannot claim the entire need circle for itself, which is why its sales potential as a rule remains clearly smaller than market potential.

The statement is false.

Absolute quantity share needs market volume. Own actual sales are related to the sales of all suppliers, not to own sales potential. Potential is an internal target figure and does not belong in this denominator. Anyone who takes potential instead of volume distorts market share. The statement names the correct reference.

The statement is true.

This point: relative market share compares own sales directly with those of the largest competitor. If own sales lie below, the quotient is smaller than one; a value above one presupposes own sales above those of the rival. Lower own sales cannot cross this threshold.

The statement is false.

title: Market leadership: absolute and relative share in interaction
context: In a value market for e-bikes of 90 million euros, company A turns over 45 million euros, the largest competitor 30 million euros and the remaining suppliers together 15 million euros. Evaluate the following statements on market leadership and market share:
statements: An absolute market share of 50 percent automatically means that the company is also relatively market leader.
A relative market share greater than one indicates that own revenue is higher than that of the previously strongest competitor.
Market leadership can as a rule be read only from absolute market share; relative market share supplies no additional information for that.
If the revenue of the largest competitor is higher than own revenue, relative market share automatically lies above one.
A company's market share may as a rule only be determined in value terms in euros, usually not in quantity terms in units.
tactical_explanations:
Absolute and relative market share are two different indicators. A company with 40 percent absolute share can nonetheless be relatively market leader if the strongest rival holds only 25 percent (40/25 > 1); conversely an absolute share of 50 percent alone says nothing yet about how high the revenue of the largest competitor is. Only the comparison of both revenues decides relative leadership.

The statement is false.

Above one means: own revenue higher than that of the strongest rival. That is the central condition of relative market leadership. The quotient of own revenue and competitor revenue then lies above one. Below one one remains behind the rival. The statement captures exactly this definition. Below one the company remains behind the rival.

The statement is true.

Relative market share supplies precisely the information that absolute share does not show: the direct comparison with the strongest rival. A high absolute share can coincide with a relative share below one if the market overall has very few but unequally large suppliers.

The statement is false.

Higher rival revenue presses the quotient below one. If the revenue of the largest competitor is higher than own, relative market share lies below one, not above. A value above one presupposes precisely the opposite. The statement asserts the wrong sign of the relation. Above one presupposes precisely higher own revenue.

The statement is false.

Market share may use quantity or value. Both calculation methods are admissible and at different average prices can lead to different percentages. "Exclusively in value terms" wrongly strikes the quantity variant. Units and euros are parallel measurement paths. The statement is therefore false. Units and euros remain parallel, equal measurement paths.

The statement is false.

title: Quantity share and value share can diverge
context: The same bicycle market comprises 200 units or 1,000 million euros. Company A sells 40 units for 280 million euros, the largest competitor 50 units for 200 million euros. Evaluate the following statements on quantity and value share:
statements: If a company sells more expensive products than the market average, its value market share can be higher than its quantity market share.
Quantity and value absolute market share must coincide when suppliers have different average prices.
A company that sells fewer units than its largest competitor can nonetheless be market leader in value terms if it achieves clearly higher prices.
Relative market share can turn out differently depending on whether it is calculated in quantity or value terms and can even lie on different sides of the threshold of one.
A company's value market share as a rule depends only on the number of units sold, not on the price achieved.
tactical_explanations:
Expensive units lift the value share. If a company sells comparatively few but expensive units, its share of total revenue can lie higher than its share of total units. Higher average prices explain the gap. Quantity and value must then be read separately. The statement describes exactly this effect.

The statement is true.

Different average prices of suppliers typically let quantity and value share diverge, not coincide. Only if all suppliers had the same average price would both calculation methods yield the same percentage. At different prices equality is the exception, not the rule.

The statement is false.

Fewer units, more revenue is possible. If revenue despite lower unit count lies above that of the largest competitor, value relative market share is above one while quantity relative can remain below one. Higher prices compensate the unit lag. The statement captures this decoupling. Higher prices can more than compensate the unit lag in revenue.

The statement is true.

Quantity and value can hit the one-threshold differently. The same supplier can lie below one in quantity terms and above one in value terms, or the reverse. Both calculation methods are independent and do not necessarily yield the same result. Suppliers' prices drive the divergence. The statement holds this possible gap.

The statement is true.

Value market share results from revenue, that is, from units times price. Two companies with the same unit count but different prices achieve different revenues and thus different value market shares. Price is therefore by no means irrelevant.

The statement is false.

title: Saturation, market share and sales potential in the same market
context: For the Austrian children's bike market: market potential 200 million euros, market volume 190 million euros, revenue company A 38 million euros, revenue largest competitor 57 million euros, sales potential company A 50 million euros. Evaluate the following statements:
statements: A market can be almost saturated even if no supplier in it is relative market leader.
A company's absolute market share is regularly calculated in relation to market potential, not to market volume.
If the revenue of the largest competitor clearly exceeds own revenue, the relative market share of the own company can nonetheless lie above one.
The sales potential of an individual company may lie above its own actual sales volume without exceeding market potential.
Even an almost saturated market can be turned back into an unsaturated market through new product variants or new target groups.
tactical_explanations:
Saturation and market leadership are independent. Saturation measures volume to potential; relative market leadership measures own revenue to the strongest rival. A market can be nearly exhausted without any supplier lying above one. Both indicators answer different questions. The statement separates them correctly.

The statement is true.

Absolute market share relates to market volume. The denominator is the actual sales of all suppliers, not theoretical market potential. Potential would be a larger reference figure and would artificially shrink the share. Anyone who always divides by potential chooses the wrong denominator. The statement is therefore false.

The statement is false.

Higher rival revenue keeps the quotient below one. Relative market share is own revenue divided by revenue of the largest competitor. If rival revenue is clearly higher, the value lies below one, not above. A value above one presupposes higher own revenue. The statement asserts the impossible. A value above one presupposes higher own than foreign revenue.

The statement is false.

A company's sales potential is the sought best case and typically lies above the sales volume actually reached, but remains below market potential, which describes the entire market. This ranking — actual sales smaller than own potential, own potential smaller than market potential — is the normal case.

The statement is true.

New variants or target groups open saturated markets. The circle of need-holders can be widened so that room between volume and potential arises again. An almost saturated state is therefore not an endpoint. The statement describes exactly this reopening. Growth remains conceivable via product and target group.

The statement is true.
